------------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m1p5t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Chassis, BaysA, BaysB

Lines == {"A", "B"}
NoTicket == [line |-> "pool", bay |-> 0]

RingSize(l) == IF l = "A" THEN BaysA ELSE BaysB
Ring(l) == 0 .. (RingSize(l) - 1)

VARIABLES tokenA, tokenB, stage, ticket, sealLog
vars == <<tokenA, tokenB, stage, ticket, sealLog>>

TokenOf(l) == IF l = "A" THEN tokenA ELSE tokenB
LogEntries == 1 .. Len(sealLog)

TypeOK ==
  /\ tokenA \in Ring("A")
  /\ tokenB \in Ring("B")
  /\ stage \in [Chassis -> {"pooled", "ticketed", "sealed", "discharged"}]
  /\ ticket \in [Chassis -> [line : Lines \cup {"pool"}, bay : 0 .. 9]]

Init ==
  /\ tokenA = 0
  /\ tokenB = 0
  /\ stage = [c \in Chassis |-> "pooled"]
  /\ ticket = [c \in Chassis |-> NoTicket]
  /\ sealLog = <<>>

AdvanceA ==
  /\ tokenA' = (tokenA + 1) % BaysA
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenB, stage, ticket, sealLog>>

AdvanceB ==
  /\ tokenB' = (tokenB + 1) % BaysB
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenA, stage, ticket, sealLog>>

\* Only the bay holding its ring's token may pull a car out of the shared pool;
\* that is what stops both lines from working the same chassis at once.
PickUp(c, l) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "pooled"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "ticketed"]
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![c] = [line |-> l, bay |-> TokenOf(l)]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenA, tokenB, sealLog>>

\* The seal guard looks only at the chassis stage, never at the log, so the
\* "at most once" claim below is a consequence of the stage machine.
SealCoat(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "ticketed"
  /\ ticket[c].bay = TokenOf(ticket[c].line)
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "sealed"]
  /\ sealLog' = Append(sealLog, [car |-> c, line |-> ticket[c].line])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenA, tokenB, ticket>>

Discharge(c) ==
  /\ stage[c] = "sealed"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "discharged"]
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![c] = NoTicket]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenA, tokenB, sealLog>>

SealAny == \E c \in Chassis : SealCoat(c)

Next ==
  \/ AdvanceA
  \/ AdvanceB
  \/ \E c \in Chassis, l \in Lines : PickUp(c, l)
  \/ SealAny
  \/ \E c \in Chassis : Discharge(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(AdvanceA)
  /\ WF_vars(AdvanceB)
  /\ SF_vars(SealAny)

\* No chassis id shows up twice in the seal log.
SealedAtMostOnce ==
  \A i, j \in LogEntries : sealLog[i].car = sealLog[j].car => i = j

\* A ticketed car keeps waiting for its own bay's token to come round again.
EveryTicketEventuallySealed ==
  \A c \in Chassis :
    (stage[c] = "ticketed") ~> (stage[c] \in {"sealed", "discharged"})
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Chassis = {c1, c2, c3}
    BaysA = 2
    BaysB = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SealedAtMostOnce

PROPERTY EveryTicketEventuallySealed
nl:
A drive-through car-wash site runs two conveyor lines, line A and line B, side by side. Both lines pull vehicles out of the same shared arrival pool, so a chassis waiting in the pool can be picked up by either line. Each line is organized as a ring of applicator bays, and a single token circulates around each ring; only the bay currently holding its line's token may act on a vehicle. The token in line A advances one bay at a time around its ring, and independently the token in line B advances around its own ring.

When the token-holding bay of a line picks up a chassis from the arrival pool, it stamps a ticket recording which line and which bay took it, and the chassis leaves the pool so the other line can no longer take it. The irreversible step is the ceramic seal coat: once a chassis has been seal-coated the finish cannot be stripped or reapplied, and every seal coat is written as an entry in the site's seal log with the chassis id and the line that did it. A chassis may only be seal-coated by the bay named on its ticket, and only while that bay is the current token holder of its line, so a chassis usually waits for its bay's token to come back around. After the seal has been applied the chassis is discharged from the line and its ticket is torn up; a discharged chassis never re-enters the arrival pool.

The full action set is: advance the token in ring A, advance the token in ring B, pick up a pooled chassis onto the token-holding bay of one of the lines, seal-coat a ticketed chassis when its bay holds the token, and discharge a sealed chassis from the line.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No chassis id ever appears in two different entries of the seal log, so the irreversible seal coat is applied to a given vehicle at most once even though two independent lines draw from the same pool.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every chassis that has been picked up and ticketed by a line is eventually seal-coated.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m6p3t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Blocks, Trains, LeaseDur, MaxTime, MaxRows

NoLease == [holder |-> "free", exp |-> 0, row |-> 0]
Idle == [blk |-> "outside", row |-> 0]

VARIABLES clock, register, radio, riding, ledger
vars == <<clock, register, radio, riding, ledger>>

Rows == 1 .. Len(ledger)

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0 .. MaxTime
  /\ register \in [Blocks -> [holder : Trains \cup {"free"}, exp : Nat, row : Nat]]
  /\ riding \in [Trains -> [blk : Blocks \cup {"outside"}, row : Nat]]

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ register = [b \in Blocks |-> NoLease]
  /\ radio = {}
  /\ riding = [t \in Trains |-> Idle]
  /\ ledger = <<>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxTime
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, radio, riding, ledger>>

\* A block may be re-leased once its filed lease has run out on the clock; the
\* old ledger row keeps its old end, so the two ranges butt up but never overlap.
IssueLease(b, t) ==
  /\ Len(ledger) < MaxRows
  /\ \/ register[b].holder = "free"
     \/ register[b].exp <= clock
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger,
        [blk |-> b, trn |-> t, start |-> clock, ends |-> clock + LeaseDur])
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![b] =
        [holder |-> t, exp |-> clock + LeaseDur, row |-> Len(ledger) + 1]]
  /\ radio' = radio \cup
        {[kind |-> "grant", blk |-> b, trn |-> t, row |-> Len(ledger) + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, riding>>

DeliverGrant(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "grant"
  /\ riding[m.trn].blk = "outside"
  /\ register[m.blk].row = m.row
  /\ clock < register[m.blk].exp
  /\ riding' = [riding EXCEPT ![m.trn] = [blk |-> m.blk, row |-> m.row]]
  /\ radio' = radio \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, register, ledger>>

HandBack(t) ==
  /\ riding[t].blk \in Blocks
  /\ radio' = radio \cup
        {[kind |-> "back", blk |-> riding[t].blk, trn |-> t, row |-> riding[t].row]}
  /\ riding' = [riding EXCEPT ![t] = Idle]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, register, ledger>>

\* The row-number test here is what stops a late hand-back from stretching a
\* long-dead ledger row forward over somebody else's lease.
DeliverBack(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "back"
  /\ register[m.blk].row = m.row
  /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![m.row].ends = clock]
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![m.blk] = NoLease]
  /\ radio' = radio \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, riding>>

DiscardStale(m) ==
  /\ register[m.blk].row # m.row
  /\ radio' = radio \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, register, riding, ledger>>

Next ==
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E b \in Blocks, t \in Trains : IssueLease(b, t)
  \/ \E m \in radio : DeliverGrant(m)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : HandBack(t)
  \/ \E m \in radio : DeliverBack(m)
  \/ \E m \in radio : DiscardStale(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Ledger rows for one block must lie in disjoint time ranges.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A i, j \in Rows :
    (i # j /\ ledger[i].blk = ledger[j].blk)
      => \/ ledger[i].ends <= ledger[j].start
         \/ ledger[j].ends <= ledger[i].start
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {north, south}
    Trains = {tr1, tr2}
    LeaseDur = 2
    MaxTime = 3
    MaxRows = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks, and a central interlocking hands out timed occupancy leases for those blocks to trains. Time is kept by a shared wall clock that ticks forward. When the interlocking leases a block to a train it stamps the lease with the current clock reading as the start and a fixed lease duration as the expiry, files the lease as a numbered row in its allocation ledger, and radios a grant to the train. The interlocking will only issue a fresh lease for a block if that block has no lease on file or the lease on file has already expired according to the clock.

Radio traffic between the interlocking and the trains is not ordered: grants and hand-backs sit in a common in-flight pool and can be picked up in any order, so an old message can surface long after the lease it refers to is history. Every message carries the ledger row number of the lease it belongs to. A train that picks up a grant moves into the block only if that row number is still the block's current lease and the clock has not passed the expiry; it remembers the row number it entered under. When a train leaves a block it radios a hand-back quoting that remembered row number. The interlocking honours a hand-back only when the quoted row number is still the block's current lease; it then closes out that ledger row by writing the current clock reading as the row's real end and marks the block free. Any message whose row number is no longer the block's current lease is thrown away by whoever picks it up.

The full action set is: tick the clock, issue a lease for a free or expired block, deliver a grant so a train enters a block, have an occupying train radio a hand-back and leave, deliver a hand-back so the interlocking closes the ledger row and frees the block, and discard a message whose row number is out of date.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Two ledger rows for the same signalling block never cover overlapping time ranges, so a block is never allocated to two trains for even an instant.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od5m8p4t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Agents, Lobbies, SeatLimit

FREE == "free"
NoAim == [lob |-> "none", seen |-> 0]

VARIABLES region, lobbyLock, step, aim, roster
vars == <<region, lobbyLock, step, aim, roster>>

Alive(a) == step[a] \notin {"dead", "retired"}

Init ==
  /\ region = FREE
  /\ lobbyLock = [l \in Lobbies |-> FREE]
  /\ step = [a \in Agents |-> "idle"]
  /\ aim = [a \in Agents |-> NoAim]
  /\ roster = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]

NameTarget(a, l) ==
  /\ step[a] = "idle"
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "queued"]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![a] = [lob |-> l, seen |-> 0]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<region, lobbyLock, roster>>

TakeRegion(a) ==
  /\ step[a] = "queued"
  /\ region = FREE
  /\ region' = a
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, aim, roster>>

\* Coarse before fine: only the region holder ever reaches for a lobby lock,
\* so the two lock levels can never be grabbed in opposite orders.
TakeLobby(a) ==
  /\ step[a] = "coarse"
  /\ lobbyLock[aim[a].lob] = FREE
  /\ lobbyLock' = [lobbyLock EXCEPT ![aim[a].lob] = a]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![a].seen = roster[aim[a].lob]]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "fine"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<region, roster>>

\* The seat count is read at lock time and written back incremented here; the
\* fine lock is the only thing keeping that read-modify-write honest.
Seat(a) ==
  /\ step[a] = "fine"
  /\ aim[a].seen < SeatLimit
  /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![aim[a].lob] = aim[a].seen + 1]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "placed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<region, lobbyLock, aim>>

Bounce(a) ==
  /\ step[a] = "fine"
  /\ aim[a].seen = SeatLimit
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "placed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<region, lobbyLock, aim, roster>>

DropLocks(a) ==
  /\ step[a] = "placed"
  /\ region' = FREE
  /\ lobbyLock' = [lobbyLock EXCEPT ![aim[a].lob] = FREE]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![a] = NoAim]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED roster

Die(a) ==
  /\ Alive(a)
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "dead"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<region, lobbyLock, aim, roster>>

Reclaim(a) ==
  /\ step[a] = "dead"
  /\ region' = IF region = a THEN FREE ELSE region
  /\ lobbyLock' = [l \in Lobbies |-> IF lobbyLock[l] = a THEN FREE ELSE lobbyLock[l]]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![a] = NoAim]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "retired"]
  /\ UNCHANGED roster

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Agents, l \in Lobbies : NameTarget(a, l)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : TakeRegion(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : TakeLobby(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : Seat(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : Bounce(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : DropLocks(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : Die(a)
  \/ \E a \in Agents : Reclaim(a)

AnyTakeLobby == \E a \in Agents : TakeLobby(a)
AnySeat == \E a \in Agents : Seat(a)
AnyBounce == \E a \in Agents : Bounce(a)
AnyDrop == \E a \in Agents : DropLocks(a)
AnyReclaim == \E a \in Agents : Reclaim(a)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(AnyTakeLobby)
  /\ WF_vars(AnySeat)
  /\ WF_vars(AnyBounce)
  /\ WF_vars(AnyDrop)
  /\ WF_vars(AnyReclaim)

SeatLimitHolds == \A l \in Lobbies : roster[l] <= SeatLimit

RegionLockAlwaysReleased == (region # FREE) ~> (region = FREE)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Agents = {a1, a2}
    Lobbies = {alpha, beta}
    SeatLimit = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatLimitHolds

PROPERTY RegionLockAlwaysReleased

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A multiplayer game matchmaker seats waiting parties into lobbies. Several matchmaker agents run at once, and to keep them from tangling they always take locks in the same order: first the coarse lock on the whole lobby region, then the fine lock on the one lobby they intend to seat into. An agent starts idle, then names the lobby it wants and joins the queue for the region lock. Once it holds the region lock it waits for that lobby's own lock; because only the region-lock holder ever reaches for a lobby lock, the agents cannot end up waiting on each other in a cycle.

Holding the lobby lock, the agent reads the lobby's current seat count and remembers it. If the remembered count is below the lobby's seat limit, the agent seats its party by writing back the remembered count plus one; the read and the write-back are only safe because the lobby lock is held throughout. If the remembered count is already at the limit the agent bounces the party instead. Either way it then drops both locks in one go and returns to idle.

Any agent can die silently at any moment, without dropping whatever locks it holds. The region watchdog notices the missing heartbeat and reclaims every lock that the dead agent was holding, after which the agent is retired for good and never acts again.

The full action set is: an idle agent names a target lobby and queues, an agent takes the coarse region lock, an agent takes the fine lock on its target lobby and reads the seat count, an agent seats its party by writing back the incremented count, an agent bounces because its target is full, an agent drops both locks and goes idle, an agent dies silently, and the watchdog reclaims a dead agent's locks and retires it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No lobby's seat count ever rises above its seat limit.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the coarse region lock is held it is eventually free again.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m1p0t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumBays

Bays == 0 .. (NumBays - 1)
Hop(i, k) == (i + k) % NumBays

VARIABLES seat, serial, badge, valve, running
vars == <<seat, serial, badge, valve, running>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ seat \in Bays
  /\ serial \in Nat
  /\ badge \in [Bays -> Nat]
  /\ valve \in [Bays -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ running \in [Bays -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ seat = 0
  /\ serial = 1
  /\ badge = [b \in Bays |-> IF b = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0]
  /\ valve = [b \in Bays |-> FALSE]
  /\ running = [b \in Bays |-> TRUE]

\* Hand-off skips dead bays: k is the shortest clockwise distance to a bay that
\* is still up, so the ring closes over the survivors.
PassToken(k) ==
  /\ k \in 1 .. (NumBays - 1)
  /\ running[Hop(seat, k)]
  /\ \A j \in 1 .. (k - 1) : ~running[Hop(seat, j)]
  /\ ~valve[seat]
  /\ seat' = Hop(seat, k)
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![Hop(seat, k)] = serial]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<serial, valve, running>>

OpenValve(b) ==
  /\ running[b]
  /\ seat = b
  /\ badge[b] = serial
  /\ ~valve[b]
  /\ valve' = [valve EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, serial, badge, running>>

CloseValve(b) ==
  /\ valve[b]
  /\ valve' = [valve EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, serial, badge, running>>

\* Losing power trips the interlock, so a dead bay is never left on the main.
LosePower(b) ==
  /\ running[b]
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ valve' = [valve EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, serial, badge>>

MintToken(b) ==
  /\ ~running[seat]
  /\ running[b]
  /\ serial' = serial + 1
  /\ seat' = b
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![b] = serial + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<valve, running>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in 1 .. (NumBays - 1) : PassToken(k)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : OpenValve(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : CloseValve(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : LosePower(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays : MintToken(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Drawing implies you hold the seat and your badge is the live serial.
OnlyTokenHolderDraws ==
  \A b \in Bays : valve[b] => (seat = b /\ badge[b] = serial)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumBays = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OnlyTokenHolderDraws

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
The wash bays along a car-wash conveyor all feed off one high-pressure water main, and the main can supply exactly one bay at a time without losing pressure. Access is arbitrated by a token that travels round the bays in a fixed ring order. The token carries a serial number. When a bay receives the token it writes the token's serial onto its own badge; a bay may open its valve onto the main only while it is the bay the token sits at and its badge still matches the serial of the token in circulation.

Passing the token means handing it to the next bay round the ring that is still running: dead bays are skipped over, and the first running bay clockwise from the current holder takes it. A bay must have closed its valve before it can pass the token on.

A bay can lose power without warning. When that happens it stops running, and its valve interlock slams the valve shut on the way down, so a dead bay is never left drawing from the main. But the token it was holding goes down with it. The ring supervisor watches for this: when the bay the token sits at is no longer running, the supervisor mints a replacement token with the next serial number up and places it at some running bay, which badges itself with the new serial. The old serial is thereby fenced off, so nothing that still believed in the old token could act on it.

The full action set is: pass the token clockwise to the next running bay, open a valve onto the main, close a valve, lose power silently with the valve interlock tripping shut, and mint a replacement token at a running bay when the current holder is dead.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bay drawing from the high-pressure main is always the bay the token currently sits at and always carries a badge matching the circulating token serial, so two bays are never on the main together.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m0p5t5 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Hotspots, Drones, MaxRecalls, MaxSorties

Loitering == [hs |-> "none", rev |-> 0]

VARIABLES rev, row, plan, sorties, missionLog
vars == <<rev, row, plan, sorties, missionLog>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ rev \in [Hotspots -> Nat]
  /\ row \in [Hotspots -> {"unspent", "flagged", "spent"}]
  /\ plan \in [Drones -> [hs : Hotspots \cup {"none"}, rev : Nat]]
  /\ sorties \in [Drones -> 0 .. MaxSorties]

Init ==
  /\ rev = [h \in Hotspots |-> 0]
  /\ row = [h \in Hotspots |-> "unspent"]
  /\ plan = [d \in Drones |-> Loitering]
  /\ sorties = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ missionLog = <<>>

TakePlan(d, h) ==
  /\ plan[d].hs = "none"
  /\ row[h] = "unspent"
  /\ sorties[d] < MaxSorties
  /\ sorties' = [sorties EXCEPT ![d] = sorties[d] + 1]
  /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![d] = [hs |-> h, rev |-> rev[h]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, row, missionLog>>

\* Releasing steps the revision as well as marking the row spent: the step is
\* what makes every other drone's copied revision go stale.
Release(d) ==
  /\ plan[d].hs \in Hotspots
  /\ plan[d].rev = rev[plan[d].hs]
  /\ row[plan[d].hs] # "flagged"
  /\ row' = [row EXCEPT ![plan[d].hs] = "spent"]
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![plan[d].hs] = rev[plan[d].hs] + 1]
  /\ missionLog' = Append(missionLog, [hs |-> plan[d].hs, by |-> d])
  /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![d] = Loitering]
  /\ UNCHANGED sorties

TearUp(d) ==
  /\ plan[d].hs \in Hotspots
  /\ \/ plan[d].rev # rev[plan[d].hs]
     \/ row[plan[d].hs] = "flagged"
  /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![d] = Loitering]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, row, sorties, missionLog>>

Resolve(d) == Release(d) \/ TearUp(d)
ResolveAny == \E d \in Drones : Resolve(d)

\* Commander overrides: a recall invalidates plans in the air by hand.
Recall(h) ==
  /\ row[h] = "unspent"
  /\ rev[h] < MaxRecalls
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![h] = rev[h] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<row, plan, sorties, missionLog>>

Flag(h) ==
  /\ row[h] = "unspent"
  /\ row' = [row EXCEPT ![h] = "flagged"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, plan, sorties, missionLog>>

Unflag(h) ==
  /\ row[h] = "flagged"
  /\ row' = [row EXCEPT ![h] = "unspent"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, plan, sorties, missionLog>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drones, h \in Hotspots : TakePlan(d, h)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Resolve(d)
  \/ \E h \in Hotspots : Recall(h)
  \/ \E h \in Hotspots : Flag(h)
  \/ \E h \in Hotspots : Unflag(h)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ResolveAny)

\* A spent hotspot leaves no live bet behind it.
NoLivePlanOnSpentRow ==
  \A d \in Drones :
    (plan[d].hs \in Hotspots /\ row[plan[d].hs] = "spent")
      => plan[d].rev # rev[plan[d].hs]

EveryPlanResolved ==
  \A d \in Drones : (plan[d].hs \in Hotspots) ~> (plan[d].hs = "none")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Hotspots = {h1, h2}
    Drones = {d1, d2}
    MaxRecalls = 2
    MaxSorties = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLivePlanOnSpentRow

PROPERTY EveryPlanResolved

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A swarm of surveillance drones circles a wildfire and works from a shared hotspot table held at the incident base. Each hotspot row carries a revision number. A drone that wants to work a hotspot reads the row and copies the revision number into its onboard plan; nothing is locked at that moment, the plan is simply a bet that the row will not have moved on by the time the drone is overhead. Every drone launches with a fixed number of sorties in it, and taking a plan burns one, so no drone can keep cycling through plans forever.

The irreversible act is the retardant release: once a hotspot has been doused the canister is gone and the ground chemistry cannot be undone, and each release is written into the mission log. A drone releases only if the revision it copied still matches the row's revision and the row is not flagged for a ground crew. A successful release marks the row spent and steps the revision number up, which is exactly what fences off any other drone still flying on the old revision. A drone whose bet has gone stale, or whose target got flagged for a ground crew, tears up its plan and goes back to loitering.

The incident commander has an override that does not play by the optimistic rules. The commander can recall a hotspot, stepping its revision number up by hand purely to invalidate every plan in the air against it; can flag a hotspot for a ground crew so no drone will douse it; and can clear that flag again later. Drones only pick up plans against hotspots that are unspent and unflagged.

The full action set is: a loitering drone with sorties left reads a hotspot row and takes a plan, a drone releases retardant when its revision still matches and the row is unflagged, a drone tears up a stale or flagged plan, the commander recalls a hotspot by stepping its revision, the commander flags a hotspot for a ground crew, and the commander clears that flag.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a hotspot has been doused, no drone anywhere is still holding a plan whose copied revision matches that row's current revision, so a second retardant release on the same hotspot can never pass the revision check.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every plan a drone takes is eventually resolved, either by releasing retardant or by being torn up.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m2p3t3 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Sites, Orders

FreeSlot == "unclaimed"

VARIABLES phase, ballot, claim, landed, register
vars == <<phase, ballot, claim, landed, register>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Orders -> {"fresh", "preparing", "committed", "aborted"}]
  /\ ballot \in [Orders -> [Sites -> {"silent", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ claim \in [Sites -> Orders \cup {FreeSlot}]
  /\ landed \in [Orders -> SUBSET Sites]
  /\ register \in [Sites -> Orders \cup {"empty"}]

Init ==
  /\ phase = [o \in Orders |-> "fresh"]
  /\ ballot = [o \in Orders |-> [s \in Sites |-> "silent"]]
  /\ claim = [s \in Sites |-> FreeSlot]
  /\ landed = [o \in Orders |-> {}]
  /\ register = [s \in Sites |-> "empty"]

OpenOrder(o) ==
  /\ phase[o] = "fresh"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "preparing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, claim, landed, register>>

\* The courier network is slow but never loses a notice, so delivery is just an
\* arbitrary delay -- there is no timeout path anywhere in this protocol.
DeliverNotice(o, s) ==
  /\ phase[o] = "preparing"
  /\ s \notin landed[o]
  /\ landed' = [landed EXCEPT ![o] = landed[o] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, claim, register>>

VoteYes(o, s) ==
  /\ s \in landed[o]
  /\ ballot[o][s] = "silent"
  /\ claim[s] = FreeSlot
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![s] = o]
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![o][s] = "yes"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, landed, register>>

VoteNo(o, s) ==
  /\ s \in landed[o]
  /\ ballot[o][s] = "silent"
  /\ claim[s] # FreeSlot
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![o][s] = "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, claim, landed, register>>

Commit(o) ==
  /\ phase[o] = "preparing"
  /\ \A s \in Sites : ballot[o][s] = "yes"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "committed"]
  /\ register' = [s \in Sites |-> o]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, claim, landed>>

\* Abort drops only the claims this order is holding; touching anybody else's
\* claim here is exactly the bug the invariant below is watching for.
Abort(o) ==
  /\ phase[o] = "preparing"
  /\ \E s \in Sites : ballot[o][s] = "no"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "aborted"]
  /\ claim' = [s \in Sites |-> IF claim[s] = o THEN FreeSlot ELSE claim[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, landed, register>>

Next ==
  \/ \E o \in Orders : OpenOrder(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Sites : DeliverNotice(o, s)
  \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Sites : VoteYes(o, s)
  \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Sites : VoteNo(o, s)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Commit(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Abort(o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A committed order must still own every site's slot claim.
CommittedOrderOwnsEverySlot ==
  \A o \in Orders :
    phase[o] = "committed" => \A s \in Sites : claim[s] = o
================================================================================
nl:
A regional blood bank tracks its inventory across several storage sites. Each site keeps one reserved slot in its cold room that a cross-site order can claim. An order that needs blood from every site is settled by a two-phase commit run by the dispatch desk.

The desk opens an order by sending a prepare notice to all sites; the notices travel over a slow internal courier network, so a site may sit for a long while before its notice reaches it. Sites are never assumed dead: the desk has no timeout and never gives up on a silent site, it simply waits for the answer to come back. When a prepare notice finally lands, the site looks at its reserved slot. If the slot is unclaimed the site claims it for that order and answers yes; if the slot is already claimed by some other order the site answers no.

The desk commits an order only when every site has answered yes, and on commit it writes that order's name into the allocation register of every site. If any site answers no, the desk aborts the order and tells the sites to drop the claims that this order and only this order was holding; claims belonging to other orders are left alone. A committed order keeps its claims permanently, because the blood has left the cold room.

The full action set is: the desk opens an order and sends prepare notices, a prepare notice is delivered to a site after an arbitrary delay, a site claims its free slot and votes yes, a site votes no because its slot is already claimed, the desk commits an order whose sites all voted yes and writes the allocation register, and the desk aborts an order that got a no and releases only that order's claims.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed order still holds the slot claim at every single site, so no site's slot can ever have been handed to a second order.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m2p6t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Lanes, Modules, MaxTicket

DeadSlip == [lane |-> "none", tkt |-> 0]

VARIABLES cycle, stamp, slip, dosing, book
vars == <<cycle, stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

\* A slip is live only while the lane it names is still on that same ticket.
LiveSlip(m) ==
  /\ slip[m].lane \in Lanes
  /\ slip[m].tkt = stamp[slip[m].lane]
  /\ cycle[slip[m].lane] \in {"preparing", "committed"}

Init ==
  /\ cycle = [l \in Lanes |-> "idle"]
  /\ stamp = [l \in Lanes |-> 0]
  /\ slip = [m \in Modules |-> DeadSlip]
  /\ dosing = [m \in Modules |-> "none"]
  /\ book = 1

OpenCycle(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "idle"
  /\ book <= MaxTicket
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "preparing"]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![l] = book]
  /\ book' = book + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slip, dosing>>

\* Enrolment overwrites whatever dead slip the module was carrying.
Enrol(m, l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "preparing"
  /\ ~LiveSlip(m)
  /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![m] = [lane |-> l, tkt |-> stamp[l]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cycle, stamp, dosing, book>>

CommitCycle(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "preparing"
  /\ \A m \in Modules : LiveSlip(m) /\ slip[m].lane = l
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

AbortCycle(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "preparing"
  /\ \E m \in Modules : LiveSlip(m) /\ slip[m].lane # l
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

BeginDose(m) ==
  /\ dosing[m] = "none"
  /\ LiveSlip(m)
  /\ cycle[slip[m].lane] = "committed"
  /\ dosing' = [dosing EXCEPT ![m] = slip[m].lane]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cycle, stamp, slip, book>>

EndDose(m) ==
  /\ dosing[m] \in Lanes
  /\ dosing' = [dosing EXCEPT ![m] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cycle, stamp, slip, book>>

CloseOut(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ \A m \in Modules : dosing[m] # l
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

DecideStep ==
  \/ \E m \in Modules, l \in Lanes : Enrol(m, l)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : CommitCycle(l)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : AbortCycle(l)

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : OpenCycle(l)
  \/ DecideStep
  \/ \E m \in Modules : BeginDose(m)
  \/ \E m \in Modules : EndDose(m)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : CloseOut(l)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(DecideStep)

\* Nobody doses on a dead slip or on somebody else's cycle.
NoStaleDoser ==
  \A m \in Modules :
    dosing[m] \in Lanes =>
      /\ slip[m].lane = dosing[m]
      /\ slip[m].tkt = stamp[dosing[m]]
      /\ cycle[dosing[m]] = "committed"

EveryCycleDecided ==
  \A l \in Lanes :
    (cycle[l] = "preparing") ~> (cycle[l] \in {"committed", "aborted"})
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Lanes = {laneA, laneB}
    Modules = {pump, blower}
    MaxTicket = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleDoser

PROPERTY EveryCycleDecided

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash site runs two conveyor lanes that were installed independently but were plumbed into one shared pool of service modules -- the chemical pump and the air blower serve both lanes. A wash cycle on a lane can only run once every module in the pool has committed to that cycle, so each lane's controller runs the cycle as a two-phase commit over the pool.

Opening a cycle draws the next ticket number from the site's single ticket book, and the lane stamps its cycle with that ticket. A module enrols in a lane's cycle by writing down the lane and the ticket it saw; a module will only accept a new enrolment if the enrolment it is currently carrying has gone dead, meaning the lane named on it has moved on to a different ticket or is no longer running that cycle. Enrolments are never actively torn up when a cycle ends, they are simply left to go dead and get overwritten later, so stale slips are a normal sight around the site.

A lane commits its cycle once every module in the pool is carrying a live enrolment for that lane at that lane's current ticket. A lane aborts instead if some module is carrying a live enrolment belonging to the other lane. Once a lane's cycle is committed, a module may begin its dose run, and it may end that dose run afterwards. A decided cycle -- committed or aborted -- is closed out and the lane goes back to idle, but only when no module is still in the middle of a dose run for it.

The full action set is: open a cycle and draw a ticket, enrol a module whose current slip has gone dead, commit a cycle whose whole pool is live-enrolled, abort a cycle blocked by a live enrolment belonging to the other lane, begin a module's dose run, end a module's dose run, and close out a decided cycle when nothing is mid-run.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A module in the middle of a dose run is always carrying an enrolment naming the very lane it is dosing for, stamped with that lane's current ticket, and that lane's cycle is committed -- so no stale or unenrolled module ever gets to act.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every cycle that reaches the prepare stage eventually reaches a decision, either committed or aborted.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m0p0t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Techs, MaxStamp

FreeRec == [holder |-> "free", stamp |-> 0]

VARIABLES record, mode, seen, pool
vars == <<record, mode, seen, pool>>

Modes == {"away", "waiting", "attray"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ record \in [holder : Techs \cup {"free"}, stamp : 0 .. MaxStamp]
  /\ mode \in [Techs -> Modes]
  /\ seen \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxStamp]
  /\ pool \subseteq [kind : {"claim", "grant", "refuse", "handback"},
                     who : Techs, stamp : 0 .. MaxStamp]

Init ==
  /\ record = FreeRec
  /\ mode = [t \in Techs |-> "away"]
  /\ seen = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ pool = {}

ReadAndClaim(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "away"
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![t] = record.stamp]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "waiting"]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {[kind |-> "claim", who |-> t, stamp |-> record.stamp]}
  /\ UNCHANGED record

\* The compare-and-set: the record must still read free at exactly the stamp
\* the claimant copied, otherwise the claim lost its race and is refused.
GrantClaim(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "claim"
  /\ record.holder = "free"
  /\ record.stamp = m.stamp
  /\ record.stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ record' = [holder |-> m.who, stamp |-> m.stamp + 1]
  /\ pool' = (pool \ {m})
       \cup {[kind |-> "grant", who |-> m.who, stamp |-> m.stamp + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, seen>>

RefuseClaim(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "claim"
  /\ \/ record.holder # "free"
     \/ record.stamp # m.stamp
  /\ pool' = (pool \ {m})
       \cup {[kind |-> "refuse", who |-> m.who, stamp |-> m.stamp]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mode, seen>>

StepUp(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "grant"
  /\ mode[m.who] = "waiting"
  /\ m.stamp = seen[m.who] + 1
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m.who] = "attray"]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen>>

RetryAfterRefusal(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "refuse"
  /\ mode[m.who] = "waiting"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m.who] = "away"]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen>>

LosePatience(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "waiting"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "away"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen, pool>>

StepAway(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "attray"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "away"]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup
       {[kind |-> "handback", who |-> t, stamp |-> seen[t] + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen>>

\* A hand-back only counts if the record still names that tech at that stamp.
ApplyHandback(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "handback"
  /\ record.holder = m.who
  /\ record.stamp = m.stamp
  /\ record.stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ record' = [holder |-> "free", stamp |-> m.stamp + 1]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, seen>>

DiscardDead(m) ==
  /\ m.kind \in {"grant", "handback"}
  /\ \/ m.kind = "grant" /\ (mode[m.who] # "waiting" \/ m.stamp # seen[m.who] + 1)
     \/ m.kind = "handback" /\ (record.holder # m.who \/ record.stamp # m.stamp)
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mode, seen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Techs : ReadAndClaim(t) \/ LosePatience(t) \/ StepAway(t)
  \/ \E m \in pool :
       \/ GrantClaim(m) \/ RefuseClaim(m) \/ StepUp(m)
       \/ RetryAfterRefusal(m) \/ ApplyHandback(m) \/ DiscardDead(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOneAtTray ==
  \A t1, t2 \in Techs : (mode[t1] = "attray" /\ mode[t2] = "attray") => t1 = t2
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Techs = {tech1, tech2}
    MaxStamp = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT AtMostOneAtTray

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital pharmacy has one controlled-substance counting tray, and only one technician may be at that tray at any moment. There is no real lock on the tray; instead the tray controller keeps a single record holding the tray's current occupant (or the word free) and a stamp number that goes up by one every time the record changes. Technicians work optimistically against that record.

A technician who wants the tray reads the record, remembers the stamp it saw, and posts a claim carrying that stamp. All traffic between technicians and the controller sits in one message pool and is picked up in arbitrary order, so a claim, a grant, a refusal or a hand-back can be processed long after it was posted and well out of the order it was posted in.

When the controller picks up a claim it does a compare-and-set: only if the record currently reads free and its stamp is exactly the stamp on the claim does it write the claimant into the record, bump the stamp, and post a grant carrying the new stamp. Otherwise it posts a refusal. A technician steps up to the tray when it picks up a grant whose stamp is exactly one past the stamp it remembered; on picking up a refusal it goes back to reading the record and tries again. A technician waiting on an answer may also lose patience and go back to reading, leaving its old claim floating in the pool.

When a technician steps away from the tray it posts a hand-back carrying the stamp it entered under. The controller frees the record and bumps the stamp only if the record still names that technician at that same stamp. Any grant or hand-back that no longer applies is simply thrown away by whoever picks it up.

The full action set is: read the record and post a claim, compare-and-set a claim into a grant, refuse a claim that fails the compare-and-set, step up to the tray on a matching grant, go back and retry on a refusal, lose patience while waiting, step away and post a hand-back, apply a hand-back that still matches the record, and discard a message that no longer applies.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Two technicians are never at the counting tray at the same time.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m9p6t4 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Makers, MaxEpoch, MaxSlots, StartSlots

Epochs == 0 .. MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, roster, slots, badge, book, desk
vars == <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, book, desk>>

OnBook(e) == {q \in book : q.ep = e}

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in Epochs
  /\ roster \in [Epochs -> SUBSET Makers]
  /\ slots \in [Epochs -> 1 .. MaxSlots]
  /\ badge \in [Makers -> Epochs]
  /\ desk \in {"open", "settling"}

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ roster = [e \in Epochs |-> IF e = 0 THEN Makers ELSE {}]
  /\ slots = [e \in Epochs |-> StartSlots]
  /\ badge = [m \in Makers |-> 0]
  /\ book = {}
  /\ desk = "open"

\* Re-seating files a fresh roster and a fresh slot count under a new epoch;
\* the slot count may well come down, squeezing a book that was legal before.
ReSeat(p, c) ==
  /\ desk = "open"
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ p # {}
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![epoch + 1] = p]
  /\ slots' = [slots EXCEPT ![epoch + 1] = c]
  /\ desk' = "settling"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, book>>

PickUpBadge(m) ==
  /\ desk = "settling"
  /\ m \in roster[epoch]
  /\ badge[m] # epoch
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![m] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, book, desk>>

DeclareOpen ==
  /\ desk = "settling"
  /\ \A m \in roster[epoch] : badge[m] = epoch
  /\ desk' = "open"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, book>>

\* Seated and badged for this epoch, or the filing does not go on the book.
FileIndication(m) ==
  /\ desk = "open"
  /\ m \in roster[epoch]
  /\ badge[m] = epoch
  /\ Cardinality(OnBook(epoch)) < slots[epoch]
  /\ [who |-> m, ep |-> epoch] \notin book
  /\ book' = book \cup {[who |-> m, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, desk>>

PullIndication(q) ==
  /\ q \in book
  /\ book' = book \ {q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, desk>>

Settle ==
  \/ \E m \in Makers : PickUpBadge(m)
  \/ DeclareOpen

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in SUBSET Makers, c \in 1 .. MaxSlots : ReSeat(p, c)
  \/ Settle
  \/ \E m \in Makers : FileIndication(m)
  \/ \E q \in book : PullIndication(q)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Settle)

\* Each filing traces back to the roster of the epoch it was stamped with.
OnlySeatedMakersOnBook ==
  \A q \in book : q.who \in roster[q.ep]

SettlingAlwaysEnds == (desk = "settling") ~> (desk = "open")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Makers = {mmA, mmB}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxSlots = 2
    StartSlots = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OnlySeatedMakersOnBook

PROPERTY SettlingAlwaysEnds

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Before the bell, an exchange runs an opening auction in which a panel of designated market makers files indications of interest with the auction desk. The panel is not fixed: the exchange re-seats it during the session, and the number of indication slots the desk will accept for a session also changes when it re-seats. Every re-seating is stamped with a new epoch number, and the desk keeps the seated panel and the slot count for each epoch on file.

When the desk re-seats the panel it moves to the next epoch, files the new panel roster and the new slot count under that epoch, and goes into a settling state. In the settling state each newly seated market maker picks up its new badge, which is simply the epoch number it now believes it is trading under. Once every seated market maker is badged for the current epoch, the desk declares the auction open again.

A market maker may file an indication only while the desk is open, only if it is on the roster for the current epoch, and only if its own badge already reads the current epoch; a maker still carrying an old badge is stale and cannot file. Each accepted indication is filed stamped with the epoch it was accepted under. The desk refuses a filing if the number of indications already on the book for the current epoch has reached that epoch's slot count -- and because that count can be lowered at a re-seating, a book that was legal under the old configuration may leave no room at all under the new one. A market maker may also pull one of its own indications back off the book.

The full action set is: re-seat the panel with a new roster and a new slot count, badge a seated market maker for the current epoch, declare the auction open once everyone seated is badged, file an indication from a badged and seated maker while a slot is free, and pull an indication back off the book.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every indication sitting on the book was filed by a market maker who was on the roster for the very epoch that indication is stamped with.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the desk goes into settling after a re-seating, it eventually declares the auction open again.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m2p4t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Runs, Shelf, MaxBatch

VARIABLES stock, held, slot, runState, batch, wire
vars == <<stock, held, slot, runState, batch, wire>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ stock \in [Machines -> 0 .. Shelf]
  /\ held \in [Machines -> 0 .. Shelf]
  /\ slot \in [Machines -> [Runs -> {"clear", "held", "refused", "settled"}]]
  /\ runState \in [Runs -> {"draft", "asking", "commit", "abort"}]
  /\ batch \in [Runs -> 0 .. MaxBatch]

Init ==
  /\ stock = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ held = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ slot = [m \in Machines |-> [r \in Runs |-> "clear"]]
  /\ runState = [r \in Runs |-> "draft"]
  /\ batch = [r \in Runs |-> 0]
  /\ wire = {}

OpenRun(r, n) ==
  /\ runState[r] = "draft"
  /\ runState' = [runState EXCEPT ![r] = "asking"]
  /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![r] = n]
  /\ wire' = wire \cup {[tag |-> "ask", mc |-> m, run |-> r] : m \in Machines}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, held, slot>>

\* A yes vote books shelf room up front; the room stays booked until the run's
\* decision lands, which is why booked room counts against the shelf too.
BookRoom(w) ==
  /\ w.tag = "ask"
  /\ slot[w.mc][w.run] = "clear"
  /\ stock[w.mc] + held[w.mc] + batch[w.run] <= Shelf
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![w.mc] = held[w.mc] + batch[w.run]]
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![w.mc][w.run] = "held"]
  /\ wire' = (wire \ {w}) \cup {[tag |-> "yes", mc |-> w.mc, run |-> w.run]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, runState, batch>>

RefuseRoom(w) ==
  /\ w.tag = "ask"
  /\ slot[w.mc][w.run] = "clear"
  /\ stock[w.mc] + held[w.mc] + batch[w.run] > Shelf
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![w.mc][w.run] = "refused"]
  /\ wire' = (wire \ {w}) \cup {[tag |-> "no", mc |-> w.mc, run |-> w.run]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, held, runState, batch>>

DecideCommit(r) ==
  /\ runState[r] = "asking"
  /\ \A m \in Machines : [tag |-> "yes", mc |-> m, run |-> r] \in wire
  /\ runState' = [runState EXCEPT ![r] = "commit"]
  /\ wire' = (wire \ {[tag |-> "yes", mc |-> m, run |-> r] : m \in Machines})
       \cup {[tag |-> "do", mc |-> m, run |-> r] : m \in Machines}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, held, slot, batch>>

DecideAbort(r) ==
  /\ runState[r] = "asking"
  /\ \E m \in Machines : [tag |-> "no", mc |-> m, run |-> r] \in wire
  /\ runState' = [runState EXCEPT ![r] = "abort"]
  /\ wire' = (wire \ {v \in wire : v.run = r /\ v.tag \in {"yes", "no"}})
       \cup {[tag |-> "undo", mc |-> m, run |-> r] : m \in Machines}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, held, slot, batch>>

\* Decisions arrive in any order; a machine only acts on one while it still has
\* room booked for that run, so a replayed decision cannot move stock twice.
ApplyDo(w) ==
  /\ w.tag = "do"
  /\ slot[w.mc][w.run] = "held"
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![w.mc] = stock[w.mc] + batch[w.run]]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![w.mc] = held[w.mc] - batch[w.run]]
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![w.mc][w.run] = "settled"]
  /\ wire' = wire \ {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<runState, batch>>

ApplyUndo(w) ==
  /\ w.tag = "undo"
  /\ slot[w.mc][w.run] = "held"
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![w.mc] = held[w.mc] - batch[w.run]]
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![w.mc][w.run] = "settled"]
  /\ wire' = wire \ {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, runState, batch>>

DropSpent(w) ==
  /\ w.tag \in {"do", "undo"}
  /\ slot[w.mc][w.run] # "held"
  /\ wire' = wire \ {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, held, slot, runState, batch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Runs, n \in 1 .. MaxBatch : OpenRun(r, n)
  \/ \E r \in Runs : DecideCommit(r) \/ DecideAbort(r)
  \/ \E w \in wire :
       \/ BookRoom(w) \/ RefuseRoom(w) \/ ApplyDo(w)
       \/ ApplyUndo(w) \/ DropSpent(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Cans on the shelf plus room already promised never exceed the shelf.
ShelfNeverOverfilled ==
  \A m \in Machines : stock[m] + held[m] <= Shelf
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vm1, vm2}
    Runs = {r1, r2}
    Shelf = 3
    MaxBatch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ShelfNeverOverfilled

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A route operator restocks a network of vending machines from a central depot. A restock run pushes the same size batch of cans into every machine on the run, and it only happens if every machine can take it, so the depot settles each run as a two-phase commit across the machines.

Opening a run fixes the batch size and puts an ask on the wire to each machine. The wire is a shared bag of traffic with no ordering at all: asks, votes and decisions are picked off it in whatever order, and a message can sit there while other things happen around it. A machine that picks up an ask books shelf room for the batch there and then, provided the cans already on its shelf plus the room it has already booked for other runs plus this batch still fit within the shelf; it then votes yes. If they would not fit it votes no and books nothing. The booked room stays booked until that run's decision reaches the machine, which is why booked room counts against the shelf just as much as cans do.

The depot commits a run once a yes vote from every machine is on the wire, and it puts a do-it decision on the wire for each machine. If any no vote is on the wire the depot aborts, clears that run's votes off the wire, and puts an undo decision to each machine. A machine acts on a decision only while it still has room booked for that run: on do-it it moves the batch onto the shelf and gives back the booking, on undo it just gives back the booking. Either way that run's slot at that machine is marked settled, so a decision that turns up again later finds nothing booked and is thrown away.

The full action set is: open a run with a chosen batch size and ask every machine, a machine books room and votes yes, a machine votes no for want of room, the depot commits a run whose votes are all yes, the depot aborts a run that got a no, a machine applies a do-it decision, a machine applies an undo decision, and a machine throws away a decision for a slot that is already settled.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every machine, the cans on the shelf plus the shelf room currently booked for pending runs never exceed the shelf's capacity.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m5p4t3 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Doors, Hubs, HeavyDoors, LightAmps, HeavyAmps, Budget, MaxPending, MaxTries

Draw(d) == IF d \in HeavyDoors THEN HeavyAmps ELSE LightAmps

RECURSIVE Amps(_)
Amps(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET d == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN Draw(d) + Amps(S \ {d})

VARIABLES bolt, vote, tries, quiet
vars == <<bolt, vote, tries, quiet>>

Backers(d) == {h \in Hubs : vote[h] = d}
Majority(d) == 2 * Cardinality(Backers(d)) > Cardinality(Hubs)
Drawing == {d \in Doors : bolt[d] = "open"}
InFlight == {d \in Doors : bolt[d] \in {"asked", "cleared"}}

Init ==
  /\ bolt = [d \in Doors |-> "shut"]
  /\ vote = [h \in Hubs |-> "none"]
  /\ tries = [d \in Doors |-> 0]
  /\ quiet = "none"

Ask(d) ==
  /\ bolt[d] = "shut"
  /\ tries[d] < MaxTries
  /\ Cardinality(InFlight) < MaxPending
  /\ bolt' = [bolt EXCEPT ![d] = "asked"]
  /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![d] = tries[d] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, quiet>>

\* One hub at a time drifts behind the others; it never dies, it just answers
\* late, so the cluster has to wait it out rather than write it off.
GoQuiet(h) ==
  /\ quiet = "none"
  /\ quiet' = h
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bolt, vote, tries>>

CatchUp ==
  /\ quiet # "none"
  /\ quiet' = "none"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bolt, vote, tries>>

\* One vote per hub at a time: that is what stops two doors from clearing at
\* once, since their backer sets would have to overlap.
Back(h, d) ==
  /\ quiet # h
  /\ vote[h] = "none"
  /\ bolt[d] = "asked"
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![h] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bolt, tries, quiet>>

Clear(d) ==
  /\ bolt[d] = "asked"
  /\ Majority(d)
  /\ Amps(Drawing) + Draw(d) <= Budget
  /\ bolt' = [bolt EXCEPT ![d] = "cleared"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, tries, quiet>>

Refuse(d) ==
  /\ bolt[d] = "asked"
  /\ Majority(d)
  /\ Amps(Drawing) + Draw(d) > Budget
  /\ bolt' = [bolt EXCEPT ![d] = "shut"]
  /\ vote' = [h \in Hubs |-> IF vote[h] = d THEN "none" ELSE vote[h]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, quiet>>

Throw(d) ==
  /\ bolt[d] = "cleared"
  /\ bolt' = [bolt EXCEPT ![d] = "open"]
  /\ vote' = [h \in Hubs |-> IF vote[h] = d THEN "none" ELSE vote[h]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, quiet>>

Reshut(d) ==
  /\ bolt[d] = "open"
  /\ bolt' = [bolt EXCEPT ![d] = "shut"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, tries, quiet>>

Decide ==
  \/ \E h \in Hubs, d \in Doors : Back(h, d)
  \/ \E d \in Doors : Clear(d) \/ Refuse(d) \/ Throw(d) \/ Reshut(d)

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Doors : Ask(d)
  \/ \E h \in Hubs : GoQuiet(h)
  \/ CatchUp
  \/ Decide

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(CatchUp)
  /\ SF_vars(Decide)

\* The latch current of everything standing open stays inside the hub's budget.
LatchBudgetHeld == Amps(Drawing) <= Budget

EveryAskSettles == \A d \in Doors : (bolt[d] = "asked") ~> (bolt[d] # "asked")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Doors = {front, back, garage}
    Hubs = {h1, h2, h3}
    HeavyDoors = {garage}
    LightAmps = 1
    HeavyAmps = 2
    Budget = 2
    MaxPending = 2
    MaxTries = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LatchBudgetHeld

PROPERTY EveryAskSettles

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A house is wired with a small cluster of smart-home hubs that jointly control the door locks. Throwing a bolt open is not something any single hub may do: an unlock has to be backed by a majority of the hubs. The reason the hubs care is electrical, not social. Each lock's latch solenoid draws current the whole time the door stands open, the garage lock draws twice what the interior locks draw, and the low-voltage supply feeding the latches has a fixed current budget. Doors that are open together share that budget.

A door that wants to open is put up for backing, and the house never has more than a couple of unlock requests up for backing at any one time. A hub backs at most one door at a time, and its backing stays attached to that door until the request is settled; that is what keeps two doors from being cleared at the same moment, since their backer sets would have to overlap. Once a door has a majority of backers, the cluster checks whether the latch current already being drawn by the doors standing open, plus this door's own draw, would stay inside the budget. If it fits, the door is cleared; if it does not, the request is refused and the backings are handed back. A cleared door is then thrown open, at which point its backings are handed back too, and an open door is shut again later.

One hub at a time can drift behind the rest of the cluster. A hub that has drifted is not dead and is never written off: it simply cannot cast a backing until it catches up, and it always does catch up eventually.

The full action set is: put a shut door up for backing, let one hub drift behind, have the drifted hub catch up, have a hub back a door that is up for backing, clear a door that has a majority and fits in the current budget, refuse a door that has a majority but does not fit, throw a cleared door open, and shut an open door again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total latch current drawn by all the doors standing open never exceeds the low-voltage supply's budget.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every door put up for backing is eventually settled, one way or the other.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m3p1t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bays, Tickets, MaxWrites, MaxTerms

VARIABLES board, wire, confirmed, term, master
vars == <<board, wire, confirmed, term, master>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ board \in [rev : 0 .. MaxWrites, logged : SUBSET Tickets, term : 0 .. MaxTerms]
  /\ confirmed \subseteq Tickets
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerms
  /\ master \in Bays

Init ==
  /\ board = [rev |-> 0, logged |-> {}, term |-> 0]
  /\ wire = {}
  /\ confirmed = {}
  /\ term = 0
  /\ master = CHOOSE b \in Bays : TRUE

\* Failover simply anoints a new master at a higher term; the old master is not
\* told, and whatever it already put on the wire is still coming.
Failover(b) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerms
  /\ b # master
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ master' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, wire, confirmed>>

\* The master reads the tally board and posts a whole new logged set built from
\* what it just read, tagged with the revision that reading came from.
PostWrite(b, t) ==
  /\ master = b
  /\ t \notin board.logged
  /\ t \notin confirmed
  /\ ~ \E m \in wire : m.kind = "write" /\ m.tkt = t /\ m.term = term
  /\ wire' = wire \cup {[kind |-> "write", tkt |-> t, base |-> board.rev,
                         logged |-> board.logged \cup {t}, term |-> term]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, confirmed, term, master>>

\* The board takes a write only if nothing has changed under it since the read
\* and the writer is not from a superseded term.
LandWrite(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "write"
  /\ m.base = board.rev
  /\ m.term >= board.term
  /\ board.rev < MaxWrites
  /\ board' = [rev |-> board.rev + 1, logged |-> m.logged, term |-> m.term]
  /\ wire' = (wire \ {m}) \cup {[kind |-> "done", tkt |-> m.tkt]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<confirmed, term, master>>

BounceWrite(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "write"
  /\ \/ m.base # board.rev
     \/ m.term < board.term
  /\ wire' = wire \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, confirmed, term, master>>

TakeReceipt(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "done"
  /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {m.tkt}
  /\ wire' = wire \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, term, master>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bays : Failover(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays, t \in Tickets : PostWrite(b, t)
  \/ \E m \in wire : LandWrite(m) \/ BounceWrite(m) \/ TakeReceipt(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing the site has already confirmed to the crew may fall off the board.
NoLostUpdate == confirmed \subseteq board.logged
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bays = {bay1, bay2}
    Tickets = {wash1, wash2}
    MaxWrites = 3
    MaxTerms = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line keeps one shared tally board recording which wash tickets have had their undercarriage flush logged. Only the bay controller currently acting as line master is allowed to write to that board, and which controller holds that role is decided by failover: at any point the site can anoint a different bay as master under a higher term number. The bay being replaced is not told anything, so it may well still have work in the air.

To log a ticket, the master reads the tally board, takes the board's revision number and its set of logged tickets, and posts a write carrying that revision as its base, the read set plus the new ticket, and the term the master was serving under. Posted writes and the receipts that come back sit on a shared wire and are picked up in any order at all, so a write from a superseded master can turn up long after a newer write has already landed.

The board takes a write only when two things hold: the base revision on the write is still the board's current revision, meaning nothing has moved underneath the reader, and the write's term is not older than the term of the write the board last took. When it takes a write the board bumps its revision, replaces its logged set with the one carried on the write, and puts a receipt on the wire. A write failing either test is bounced off the wire and has no effect. When the site picks up a receipt it confirms that ticket to the crew, and the crew treats a confirmed ticket as done with.

The full action set is: fail over to a different bay under a higher term, the master posts a write built from a fresh read of the board, the board lands a write whose base revision and term both still check out, the board bounces a write that fails either check, and the site picks up a receipt and confirms the ticket to the crew.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every wash ticket the site has already confirmed to the crew is still present in the tally board's logged set, so no confirmed update is ever written away.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m6p5t0 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Sectors, Drones, LeaseSpan, WindowEnd

NoLease == [flyer |-> "none", ends |-> 0]

VARIABLES clock, lease, burn, flying
vars == <<clock, lease, burn, flying>>

\* A lease is live purely by the clock; nobody has to send anything to end one.
Live(s) == lease[s].flyer \in Drones /\ clock < lease[s].ends

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0 .. WindowEnd
  /\ lease \in [Sectors -> [flyer : Drones \cup {"none"}, ends : 0 .. WindowEnd]]
  /\ burn \in [Sectors -> {"unlit", "alight"}]
  /\ flying \in [Drones -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ lease = [s \in Sectors |-> NoLease]
  /\ burn = [s \in Sectors |-> "unlit"]
  /\ flying = [d \in Drones |-> TRUE]

Tick ==
  /\ clock < WindowEnd
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, burn, flying>>

\* Leases are cut so they always run out inside the operational window.
Grant(s, d) ==
  /\ burn[s] = "unlit"
  /\ ~Live(s)
  /\ flying[d]
  /\ clock + LeaseSpan <= WindowEnd
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [flyer |-> d, ends |-> clock + LeaseSpan]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, burn, flying>>

\* The one-way door: lighting hands the lease straight back, and a sector that
\* is alight can never be granted again.
Light(s, d) ==
  /\ Live(s)
  /\ lease[s].flyer = d
  /\ flying[d]
  /\ burn[s] = "unlit"
  /\ burn' = [burn EXCEPT ![s] = "alight"]
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = NoLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, flying>>

HandBack(s, d) ==
  /\ Live(s)
  /\ lease[s].flyer = d
  /\ flying[d]
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = NoLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, burn, flying>>

GoDark(d) ==
  /\ flying[d]
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, burn>>

Next ==
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E s \in Sectors, d \in Drones : Grant(s, d) \/ Light(s, d) \/ HandBack(s, d)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : GoDark(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Tick)

\* Alight sectors carry no live lease, so nobody can light one twice.
LitSectorHasNoLiveLease == \A s \in Sectors : burn[s] = "alight" => ~Live(s)

EveryLeaseRunsOut == \A s \in Sectors : Live(s) ~> ~Live(s)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Sectors = {sec1, sec2}
    Drones = {alpha, bravo}
    LeaseSpan = 2
    WindowEnd = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LitSectorHasNoLiveLease

PROPERTY EveryLeaseRunsOut

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A surveillance drone swarm works a wildfire perimeter divided into sectors. Ground crews want defensive backburns lit in some sectors, and lighting a backburn is a one-way door: once a sector's backburn is alight the fuel there is gone and the sector can never be lit again.

The base grants a drone a timed lease over a sector. The lease is stamped with an expiry read off the incident clock, and the base only grants a lease it can be sure will run out before the incident clock reaches the end of the operational window. A lease is live while it names a drone and the clock has not yet reached its expiry; once the clock passes the expiry the lease is simply dead, no message required. The base will only grant a lease over a sector that is still unlit and has no live lease on it.

A drone holding a live lease over an unlit sector may light the backburn there. Lighting it marks the sector alight and gives the lease straight back, so the sector ends up alight with nothing leased on it. A drone that decides not to light may also hand the lease back early. The incident clock ticks forward through the operational window.

Drones can fail silently: one may simply go dark mid-flight, without handing anything back and without telling anyone. A dark drone never acts again, so a sector it was holding stays leased to a ghost until the clock walks past the lease expiry, at which point the lease is dead and the base is free to grant the sector to somebody else.

The full action set is: tick the incident clock, grant a lease over an unlit sector with no live lease, light the backburn under a live lease and hand the lease back, hand a live lease back without lighting anything, and go dark.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A sector whose backburn is alight never has a live lease on it, so no drone is ever in a position to light the same sector a second time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every live lease eventually stops being live.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m1p2t4 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumBranches, Copies, MaxShelfHolds, MaxTransfers

Branches == 0 .. (NumBranches - 1)
NextBranch(b) == (b + 1) % NumBranches

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[b] + Tally(f, S \ {b})

VARIABLES onShelf, inVan, onHold, holdCap, token, transfers
vars == <<onShelf, inVan, onHold, holdCap, token, transfers>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ onShelf \in [Branches -> 0 .. Copies]
  /\ inVan \in [Branches -> 0 .. Copies]
  /\ onHold \in [Branches -> 0 .. Copies]
  /\ holdCap \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxShelfHolds]
  /\ token \in Branches
  /\ transfers \in 0 .. MaxTransfers

Init ==
  /\ onShelf = [b \in Branches |-> IF b = 0 THEN Copies ELSE 0]
  /\ inVan = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
  /\ onHold = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
  /\ holdCap = [b \in Branches |-> MaxShelfHolds]
  /\ token = 0
  /\ transfers = 0

\* Only the branch holding the token touches stock, and the token keeps moving
\* round the ring whether or not that branch has anything to do.
PassToken ==
  /\ token' = NextBranch(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, inVan, onHold, holdCap, transfers>>

SendOut(dst) ==
  /\ onShelf[token] > 0
  /\ dst # token
  /\ transfers < MaxTransfers
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![token] = onShelf[token] - 1]
  /\ inVan' = [inVan EXCEPT ![dst] = inVan[dst] + 1]
  /\ transfers' = transfers + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onHold, holdCap, token>>

TakeDelivery ==
  /\ inVan[token] > 0
  /\ inVan' = [inVan EXCEPT ![token] = inVan[token] - 1]
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![token] = onShelf[token] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onHold, holdCap, token, transfers>>

\* The hold shelf is resized while the system runs; shrinking it below what is
\* already sitting there blocks new holds but never sheds a copy.
PlaceOnHold ==
  /\ onShelf[token] > 0
  /\ onHold[token] < holdCap[token]
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![token] = onShelf[token] - 1]
  /\ onHold' = [onHold EXCEPT ![token] = onHold[token] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inVan, holdCap, token, transfers>>

ExpireHold ==
  /\ onHold[token] > 0
  /\ onHold' = [onHold EXCEPT ![token] = onHold[token] - 1]
  /\ onShelf' = [onShelf EXCEPT ![token] = onShelf[token] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inVan, holdCap, token, transfers>>

Resize(b, c) ==
  /\ holdCap[b] # c
  /\ holdCap' = [holdCap EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, inVan, onHold, token, transfers>>

Next ==
  \/ PassToken
  \/ \E d \in Branches : SendOut(d)
  \/ TakeDelivery
  \/ PlaceOnHold
  \/ ExpireHold
  \/ \E b \in Branches, c \in 0 .. MaxShelfHolds : Resize(b, c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ SF_vars(TakeDelivery)

\* Every copy is on a shelf, in a van, or on a hold shelf -- never anywhere else.
CopiesConserved ==
  Tally(onShelf, Branches) + Tally(inVan, Branches) + Tally(onHold, Branches)
    = Copies

EveryVanUnloaded == \A b \in Branches : (inVan[b] > 0) ~> (inVan[b] = 0)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumBranches = 3
    Copies = 2
    MaxShelfHolds = 2
    MaxTransfers = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CopiesConserved

PROPERTY EveryVanUnloaded
nl:
A county library system moves copies of a title around its branches. Every copy of the title is always in exactly one of three places: sitting on a branch's open shelf, riding in a van bound for a branch, or waiting on a branch's hold shelf for the patron who reserved it. Copies are never bought or withdrawn during the day, so whatever the system does, the same copies are still out there somewhere.

Stock is only ever touched by the branch that currently holds the circulation token. The token travels round the branches in a fixed ring order and keeps moving whether or not the branch holding it has anything to do. The branch with the token may send a shelf copy out in a van to another branch, may take a copy off a van that has arrived for it and put it on the shelf, may move a shelf copy onto its hold shelf for a patron, or may let a hold lapse and put that copy back on the open shelf. There is a cap on how many transfers the system will run in a day.

Each branch's hold shelf has a size, and the system resizes hold shelves while it is running -- a branch's hold shelf can be made bigger or smaller at any moment. Shrinking a hold shelf below the number of copies already sitting on it does not throw anything away; it simply means no further holds can be placed there until some lapse.

The full action set is: pass the circulation token to the next branch in the ring, send a shelf copy out in a van to another branch, take delivery of a van copy onto the shelf, move a shelf copy onto the hold shelf while it has room, let a hold lapse back onto the shelf, and resize a branch's hold shelf.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of copies on shelves, in vans, and on hold shelves always adds up to exactly the number of copies the system started with.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every van copy waiting at a branch is eventually taken in.
