----------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m3p3t2 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Posts, Controllers, Slots, MaxTerm

Unbooked == [post |-> "free", term |-> 0]

VARIABLES book, term, orbit, lead
vars == <<book, term, orbit, lead>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ book \in [Slots -> [post : Posts \cup {"free"}, term : 0 .. MaxTerm]]
  /\ term \in [Posts -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
  /\ orbit \in [Posts -> SUBSET Slots]
  /\ lead \in [Posts -> Controllers]

Init ==
  /\ book = [s \in Slots |-> Unbooked]
  /\ term = [p \in Posts |-> 0]
  /\ orbit = [p \in Posts |-> {}]
  /\ lead = [p \in Posts |-> CHOOSE c \in Controllers : TRUE]

\* Failing over drops the command link, so the post's drones break orbit before
\* the new lead starts work; nothing keeps flying on a term that just died.
FailOver(p, c) ==
  /\ term[p] < MaxTerm
  /\ c # lead[p]
  /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![p] = term[p] + 1]
  /\ lead' = [lead EXCEPT ![p] = c]
  /\ orbit' = [orbit EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED book

\* A lead can re-book a slot its own post already holds under a dead term, but
\* never one standing against the other post.
Book(p, c, s) ==
  /\ lead[p] = c
  /\ book[s].post \in {"free", p}
  /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![s] = [post |-> p, term |-> term[p]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, orbit, lead>>

GiveBack(p, c, s) ==
  /\ lead[p] = c
  /\ book[s].post = p
  /\ s \notin orbit[p]
  /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![s] = Unbooked]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, orbit, lead>>

EnterSlot(p, s) ==
  /\ book[s].post = p
  /\ book[s].term = term[p]
  /\ s \notin orbit[p]
  /\ orbit' = [orbit EXCEPT ![p] = orbit[p] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, term, lead>>

LeaveSlot(p, s) ==
  /\ s \in orbit[p]
  /\ orbit' = [orbit EXCEPT ![p] = orbit[p] \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, term, lead>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Posts, c \in Controllers : FailOver(p, c)
  \/ \E p \in Posts, c \in Controllers, s \in Slots : Book(p, c, s) \/ GiveBack(p, c, s)
  \/ \E p \in Posts, s \in Slots : EnterSlot(p, s) \/ LeaveSlot(p, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anything in the air is standing on a live booking of its own post.
NoSlotFlownTwice ==
  \A p \in Posts :
    \A s \in orbit[p] :
      book[s].post = p /\ book[s].term = term[p]
================================================================================
nl:
Two incident command posts, one on the ridge and one in the valley, each fly their own group of surveillance drones over the same wildfire. The posts were stood up independently and answer to different agencies, but the airspace over the fire is carved into a single shared pool of orbit slots, and both posts book slots out of that one pool through a common airspace register.

Each post runs its own leader election: at any moment one of its controllers is the post's lead, serving under a term number, and only the lead may book or give back slots on behalf of that post. When a post fails over it moves to a higher term and hands the lead to a different controller. Failing over is not free: the command link drops, so every drone that post had in orbit breaks off and returns to the holding pattern before the new lead takes over.

The airspace register records, for each slot, which post holds it and the term that post's lead held it under. A lead may book a slot that the register shows as free, and may also re-book a slot the register already shows against its own post under an older term, which is how a post recovers its bookings after a failover. A lead may never book a slot the register shows against the other post. Giving a slot back is only allowed once no drone from that post is orbiting in it. A drone may enter a slot only while the register shows that slot against its own post at its post's current term, and may leave a slot at any time.

The full action set is: fail a post over to a new lead under a higher term, breaking all of that post's orbits; book a slot that is free or already stands against the booking post; give back a slot with nothing orbiting in it; put a drone into a slot the register currently shows against that post at its current term; and take a drone out of a slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot with a drone orbiting in it stands in the airspace register against that drone's own command post at that post's current term, so the two posts can never both be flying the same slot.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m0p6t0 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Jobs, Presses, MaxStamp

NoBid == [job |-> "none", stamp |-> 0]

VARIABLES assigned, working, stamp, bid, powered
vars == <<assigned, working, stamp, bid, powered>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ assigned \in [Jobs -> Presses \cup {"none"}]
  /\ working \in [Presses -> Jobs \cup {"none"}]
  /\ stamp \in [Jobs -> 0 .. MaxStamp]
  /\ bid \in [Presses -> [job : Jobs \cup {"none"}, stamp : 0 .. MaxStamp]]
  /\ powered \in [Presses -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ assigned = [j \in Jobs |-> "none"]
  /\ working = [p \in Presses |-> "none"]
  /\ stamp = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
  /\ bid = [p \in Presses |-> NoBid]
  /\ powered = [p \in Presses |-> TRUE]

\* Nothing is locked when a press reads a spool entry; it just copies the stamp
\* and hopes the entry has not moved by the time it tries to take it.
ReadEntry(p, j) ==
  /\ powered[p]
  /\ working[p] = "none"
  /\ bid[p].job = "none"
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![p] = [job |-> j, stamp |-> stamp[j]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, working, stamp, powered>>

\* Taking the entry sets the spool side and the press side in one step, which is
\* the only reason the two views can be trusted to agree.
TakeEntry(p) ==
  /\ powered[p]
  /\ bid[p].job \in Jobs
  /\ stamp[bid[p].job] = bid[p].stamp
  /\ assigned[bid[p].job] = "none"
  /\ stamp[bid[p].job] < MaxStamp
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![bid[p].job] = p]
  /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p] = bid[p].job]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![bid[p].job] = stamp[bid[p].job] + 1]
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![p] = NoBid]
  /\ UNCHANGED powered

DropBid(p) ==
  /\ bid[p].job \in Jobs
  /\ \/ stamp[bid[p].job] # bid[p].stamp
     \/ assigned[bid[p].job] # "none"
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![p] = NoBid]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, working, stamp, powered>>

FinishRun(p) ==
  /\ powered[p]
  /\ working[p] \in Jobs
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![working[p]] = "none"]
  /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, bid, powered>>

\* A press can lose power mid-run without telling anyone; its rollers stop.
LosePower(p) ==
  /\ powered[p]
  /\ powered' = [powered EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, stamp, bid>>

Reclaim(j) ==
  /\ assigned[j] \in Presses
  /\ ~powered[assigned[j]]
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![j] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<working, stamp, bid, powered>>

Release ==
  \/ \E p \in Presses : FinishRun(p)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Reclaim(j)

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Presses, j \in Jobs : ReadEntry(p, j)
  \/ \E p \in Presses : TakeEntry(p) \/ DropBid(p) \/ LosePower(p)
  \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Release)

\* A powered press only ever runs a job the spool has assigned to it.
NoUnassignedPressRuns ==
  \A p \in Presses :
    (powered[p] /\ working[p] \in Jobs) => assigned[working[p]] = p

EveryClaimedJobFreedAgain ==
  \A j \in Jobs : (assigned[j] # "none") ~> (assigned[j] = "none")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Jobs = {flyer, poster}
    Presses = {pressX, pressY}
    MaxStamp = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoUnassignedPressRuns

PROPERTY EveryClaimedJobFreedAgain

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A print shop spools its jobs on a shared board, one entry per job. Presses help themselves to work off that board, and nothing on the board is ever locked. A press with nothing on its rollers reads an entry and copies down the entry's stamp number, which is simply the shop's way of noticing that an entry has moved on since somebody last looked at it.

To actually take the job, the press does a single combined step: it checks that the entry's stamp is still the one it copied and that the entry is still unassigned, and if both hold it writes itself into the entry as the assigned press, bumps the stamp, and puts the job on its own rollers. Doing the spool side and the press side together in one step is the only reason the two views of who is running what can be trusted to agree. If the stamp has moved or somebody else got there first, the press throws away what it copied and can start over from a fresh read.

A press that finishes a run clears the entry back to unassigned and comes off the job. A press can also lose power without warning, mid-run, telling nobody: its rollers stop, so it is no longer running anything, but the spool board still shows the job assigned to it. The shop's spool keeper reclaims a job whose assigned press has lost power, clearing the entry back to unassigned so another press can read it. The spool keeper only ever reclaims from a press that has actually lost power; it never pulls a job out from under a press that is still turning.

The full action set is: read a spool entry and copy its stamp, take an entry whose stamp and assignment still check out, throw away a bid that has gone stale, finish a run and clear the entry, lose power mid-run, and reclaim a job whose assigned press has lost power.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A press that still has power is never running a job unless the spool board has that job assigned to that very press.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every job that gets assigned to a press eventually becomes unassigned again.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m3p5t0 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Hubs, Locks, MaxTerm

VARIABLES term, chair, alive, fuse, receipt, wire
vars == <<term, chair, alive, fuse, receipt, wire>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ chair \in Hubs
  /\ alive \in [Hubs -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ fuse \in [Locks -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
  /\ receipt \in [Hubs -> [Locks -> 0 .. MaxTerm]]

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ chair = CHOOSE h \in Hubs : TRUE
  /\ alive = [h \in Hubs |-> TRUE]
  /\ fuse = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
  /\ receipt = [h \in Hubs |-> [l \in Locks |-> 0]]
  /\ wire = {}

Failover(h) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ alive[h]
  /\ h # chair
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ chair' = h
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, fuse, receipt, wire>>

\* Rekeying blows a physical fuse in the lock: the fuse can only ever be blown
\* once, and the announcement goes out in the same breath as the blow. Sending
\* word first and blowing afterwards is exactly what would break the property.
BlowFuse(l) ==
  /\ alive[chair]
  /\ fuse[l] = 0
  /\ term > 0
  /\ fuse' = [fuse EXCEPT ![l] = term]
  /\ wire' = wire \cup {[hub |-> h, lock |-> l, term |-> term] : h \in Hubs}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chair, alive, receipt>>

HearWord(w) ==
  /\ alive[w.hub]
  /\ receipt[w.hub][w.lock] = 0
  /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![w.hub][w.lock] = w.term]
  /\ wire' = wire \ {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chair, alive, fuse>>

\* A hub that missed the word can read the blown fuse straight off the lock.
PollLock(h, l) ==
  /\ alive[h]
  /\ fuse[l] # 0
  /\ receipt[h][l] = 0
  /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![h][l] = fuse[l]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chair, alive, fuse, wire>>

DropDead(h) ==
  /\ alive[h]
  /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![h] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chair, fuse, receipt, wire>>

Next ==
  \/ \E h \in Hubs : Failover(h) \/ DropDead(h)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : BlowFuse(l)
  \/ \E w \in wire : HearWord(w)
  \/ \E h \in Hubs, l \in Locks : PollLock(h, l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every receipt anywhere in the cluster names the same rekey as the fuse does,
\* so the cluster has only ever witnessed one rekey of any given lock.
ReceiptsNameTheOneRekey ==
  \A h \in Hubs :
    \A l \in Locks :
      receipt[h][l] # 0 => receipt[h][l] = fuse[l]
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Hubs = {hubA, hubB}
    Locks = {frontDoor, patioDoor}
    MaxTerm = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ReceiptsNameTheOneRekey

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A house runs a small cluster of smart-home hubs over its door locks. At any moment one hub is the chair of the cluster, serving under a term number, and only the chair may order a lock rekeyed. When the cluster fails over it moves to a higher term and a different hub takes the chair.

Rekeying a lock is a one-way step. It blows a physical fuse inside the lock, wiping the old pairing material for good; the fuse can only ever be blown once, and the lock stamps the term of the chair that blew it into the fuse record. The blow and the announcement to the hubs happen in the same breath: the lock cannot be rekeyed without word of that exact rekey going out, and word cannot go out ahead of the blow. Sending word first and blowing afterwards is precisely the ordering that would let a failover slip a second, differently stamped rekey in between.

Announcements sit on the house bus until a hub picks one up. A hub that picks up word of a rekey it has no record of writes down the term carried in that word. A hub that missed the word altogether can instead read the blown fuse straight off the lock and write down what it finds there. Once a hub has a record for a lock it keeps it.

Hubs can also fail silently: a hub simply stops responding, without saying so and without giving up the chair if it had it. A dead hub never picks up word, never polls a lock, and never takes the chair again, and if it was the chair the cluster has to fail over to a live hub before any more rekeying can happen.

The full action set is: fail over to a live hub under a higher term, blow a lock's fuse and announce that rekey in one step, pick word up off the bus and record it, poll a lock directly and record its blown fuse, and fail silently.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every rekey record held by any hub names the same rekey as the lock's own fuse does, so the cluster has never witnessed a lock being rekeyed more than once.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m2p5t2 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Machines, Orders

VARIABLES stage, slot, settled, chute
vars == <<stage, slot, settled, chute>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ stage \in [Desks -> [Orders -> {"idle", "asking", "closed"}]]
  /\ slot \in [Machines -> [Orders -> Desks \cup {"free"}]]
  /\ settled \subseteq Orders
  /\ chute \subseteq [ord : Orders, desk : Desks]

Init ==
  /\ stage = [d \in Desks |-> [o \in Orders |-> "idle"]]
  /\ slot = [m \in Machines |-> [o \in Orders |-> "free"]]
  /\ settled = {}
  /\ chute = {}

OpenSettlement(d, o) ==
  /\ stage[d][o] = "idle"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![d][o] = "asking"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slot, settled, chute>>

\* A machine reserves its slot for whichever desk asks first; a desk that finds
\* a slot already taken by the other desk is out of luck for that order.
Reserve(m, d, o) ==
  /\ stage[d][o] = "asking"
  /\ slot[m][o] = "free"
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![m][o] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, settled, chute>>

\* The vend is the irreversible bit: the can drops and the card is captured.
\* Unanimous reservations are not enough on their own -- the order must also
\* not already be on the settled list, because slots are freed after a vend.
Vend(d, o) ==
  /\ stage[d][o] = "asking"
  /\ \A m \in Machines : slot[m][o] = d
  /\ o \notin settled
  /\ chute' = chute \cup {[ord |-> o, desk |-> d]}
  /\ settled' = settled \cup {o}
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![d][o] = "closed"]
  /\ slot' = [m \in Machines |-> [slot[m] EXCEPT ![o] = "free"]]

WalkAway(d, o) ==
  /\ stage[d][o] = "asking"
  /\ \/ \E m \in Machines : slot[m][o] \notin {"free", d}
     \/ o \in settled
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![d][o] = "closed"]
  /\ slot' = [m \in Machines |-> [slot[m] EXCEPT ![o] =
                 IF slot[m][o] = d THEN "free" ELSE slot[m][o]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<settled, chute>>

ClearSlot(m, o) ==
  /\ slot[m][o] \in Desks
  /\ stage[slot[m][o]][o] = "closed"
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![m][o] = "free"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, settled, chute>>

Turn ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines, d \in Desks, o \in Orders : Reserve(m, d, o)
  \/ \E d \in Desks, o \in Orders : Vend(d, o) \/ WalkAway(d, o)

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Desks, o \in Orders : OpenSettlement(d, o)
  \/ Turn
  \/ \E m \in Machines, o \in Orders : ClearSlot(m, o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Turn)

\* One drop per order, no matter which desk got there.
NothingVendedTwice ==
  \A v1, v2 \in chute : v1.ord = v2.ord => v1 = v2

EverySettlementCloses ==
  \A d \in Desks :
    \A o \in Orders :
      (stage[d][o] = "asking") ~> (stage[d][o] = "closed")
================================================================================
nl:
A snack-vending operator runs two settlement desks, one east and one west, that were bought from different vendors and know nothing about each other. Both of them settle customer orders against the same shared pool of vending bays. An order is only good if every bay in the pool takes part, so each desk settles an order as a two-phase commit over the bays.

A desk opens a settlement for an order and then asks the bays to reserve their slot for that order. A bay hands its slot to whichever desk asks first, and a desk that finds a slot already reserved by the other desk has lost that order.

The vend is the irreversible step: the can drops into the chute and the customer's card is captured, and neither can be taken back. Every vend is written into the chute record with the order and the desk that did it. Having every bay's slot reserved is not by itself enough to vend, because slots are handed back as soon as a vend completes and could therefore be gathered up a second time; the desk must also find the order absent from the operator's settled list. A desk gives up on an order if some bay's slot is held by the other desk, or if the order already appears on the settled list, and giving up hands back only the slots that desk itself was holding. A bay may also clear a slot whose desk has finished with the order either way.

The full action set is: a desk opens a settlement for an order, a bay reserves its slot for the desk that asked, a desk vends an order it has unanimously reserved and that is not yet settled, a desk gives up an order that is blocked or already settled and hands back its own slots, and a bay clears a slot belonging to a desk that has finished.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The chute record never holds two entries for the same order, so no order is ever vended twice even though two independent desks work the same pool of bays.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every settlement a desk opens is eventually closed out.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m5p6t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Registrars, Units, MaxRound

VARIABLES round, pledge, slips, issued, fridge
vars == <<round, pledge, slips, issued, fridge>>

SlipsFor(b, u) == {s \in slips : s.rnd = b /\ s.unit = u}
Quorum(b, u) == 2 * Cardinality(SlipsFor(b, u)) > Cardinality(Registrars)

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 0 .. MaxRound
  /\ pledge \in [Registrars -> 0 .. MaxRound]
  /\ slips \subseteq [reg : Registrars, rnd : 1 .. MaxRound, unit : Units]
  /\ issued \subseteq [rnd : 1 .. MaxRound, unit : Units]
  /\ fridge \subseteq Units

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ pledge = [r \in Registrars |-> 0]
  /\ slips = {}
  /\ issued = {}
  /\ fridge = Units

OpenRound ==
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, slips, issued, fridge>>

\* A registrar that pledges to the open round will not sign for an older one,
\* but the slips it already signed are still lying around on the bench.
Pledge(r) ==
  /\ pledge[r] < round
  /\ pledge' = [pledge EXCEPT ![r] = round]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, slips, issued, fridge>>

SignSlip(r, u) ==
  /\ pledge[r] = round
  /\ round > 0
  /\ u \in fridge
  /\ slips' = slips \cup {[reg |-> r, rnd |-> round, unit |-> u]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, pledge, issued, fridge>>

\* Slips are picked up off the bench in no particular order and old slips look
\* just like new ones, so the round on the slip has to be read every time.
IssueUnit(u) ==
  /\ round > 0
  /\ u \in fridge
  /\ Quorum(round, u)
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {[rnd |-> round, unit |-> u]}
  /\ fridge' = fridge \ {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, pledge, slips>>

ReturnUnit(u) ==
  /\ u \notin fridge
  /\ fridge' = fridge \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, pledge, slips, issued>>

Next ==
  \/ OpenRound
  \/ \E r \in Registrars : Pledge(r)
  \/ \E r \in Registrars, u \in Units : SignSlip(r, u)
  \/ \E u \in Units : IssueUnit(u) \/ ReturnUnit(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every issue on the record is backed by a majority of slips signed in that
\* very round for that very unit -- slips from other rounds do not count.
NoIssueWithoutFreshQuorum ==
  \A a \in issued : Quorum(a.rnd, a.unit)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Registrars = {regA, regB, regC}
    Units = {bagO, bagAB}
    MaxRound = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoIssueWithoutFreshQuorum

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood bank tracks its fridge inventory through a small board of registrars, and no unit leaves the fridge on one person's say-so: issuing a unit needs a majority of the registrars to have signed for it. The board works in numbered rounds, and the bank opens a new round whenever it needs to.

A registrar pledges itself to the round that is currently open, and once pledged it will not sign anything for an older round. But pledging does not retract anything: every slip that registrar already signed in earlier rounds is still lying on the bench. A pledged registrar signs a slip for a unit that is still in the fridge; the slip carries the registrar's name, the round it was signed in, and the unit it is for.

Slips are picked up off the bench in no particular order at all, and a slip signed two rounds ago looks exactly like one signed a minute ago. That is why the round written on a slip has to be read every single time slips are counted: a unit is only issued when a majority of the registrars have slips for that unit signed in the round that is currently open. Issuing takes the unit out of the fridge and writes the issue into the record with the round it went out under. A unit that was issued and not used can be put back into the fridge, and it can then be signed for and issued again in some later round.

The full action set is: open a new round, pledge a registrar to the open round, have a pledged registrar sign a slip for a unit in the fridge, issue a unit that has a majority of slips signed in the open round, and return an issued unit to the fridge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every issue in the record is backed by a majority of slips signed for that very unit in that very round, so slips from a stale round or for another unit can never authorise a release.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p6t4 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Boxes, Techs, MaxGen, MaxWindow, MaxFlight

NoRead == [box |-> "none", gen |-> 0]

VARIABLES tag, readout, journal, outbox, window
vars == <<tag, readout, journal, outbox, window>>

InService == {b \in Boxes : tag[b].who # "none"}
LastGen(b) == IF journal[b] = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE journal[b][Len(journal[b])].gen

TypeOK ==
  /\ tag \in [Boxes -> [who : Techs \cup {"none"}, gen : 0 .. MaxGen]]
  /\ readout \in [Techs -> [box : Boxes \cup {"none"}, gen : 0 .. MaxGen]]
  /\ window \in 0 .. MaxWindow

\* Held down so the model stays small: only a couple of price sheets are ever
\* in flight across the fleet at once.
BoundedFlight == Cardinality(outbox) <= MaxFlight

Init ==
  /\ tag = [b \in Boxes |-> [who |-> "none", gen |-> 0]]
  /\ readout = [t \in Techs |-> NoRead]
  /\ journal = [b \in Boxes |-> <<>>]
  /\ outbox = {}
  /\ window = MaxWindow

ReadTag(t, b) ==
  /\ readout[t].box = "none"
  /\ readout' = [readout EXCEPT ![t] = [box |-> b, gen |-> tag[b].gen]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, journal, outbox, window>>

\* The swap only goes through if the tag still reads exactly what the tech saw:
\* free, and at the same generation. Anything else and the read is torn up.
Swap(t) ==
  /\ readout[t].box \in Boxes
  /\ tag[readout[t].box].who = "none"
  /\ tag[readout[t].box].gen = readout[t].gen
  /\ tag[readout[t].box].gen < MaxGen
  /\ Cardinality(InService) < window
  /\ tag' = [tag EXCEPT ![readout[t].box] =
        [who |-> t, gen |-> readout[t].gen + 1]]
  /\ readout' = [readout EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, outbox, window>>

TearUpRead(t) ==
  /\ readout[t].box \in Boxes
  /\ \/ tag[readout[t].box].who # "none"
     \/ tag[readout[t].box].gen # readout[t].gen
     \/ Cardinality(InService) >= window
  /\ readout' = [readout EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, journal, outbox, window>>

QueuePush(t, b) ==
  /\ tag[b].who = t
  /\ outbox' = outbox \cup {[box |-> b, gen |-> tag[b].gen, who |-> t]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, journal, window>>

\* A pushed price sheet can turn up at the box long after its author lost the
\* tag, so the box only writes it down if its generation beats the last one in.
LandPush(p) ==
  /\ p.gen > LastGen(p.box)
  /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![p.box] =
        Append(journal[p.box], [gen |-> p.gen, who |-> p.who])]
  /\ outbox' = outbox \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, window>>

BinPush(p) ==
  /\ p.gen <= LastGen(p.box)
  /\ outbox' = outbox \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, journal, window>>

HandBack(t, b) ==
  /\ tag[b].who = t
  /\ tag' = [tag EXCEPT ![b].who = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<readout, journal, outbox, window>>

\* The dispatcher widens or narrows the service window while the day runs.
Resize(c) ==
  /\ c # window
  /\ window' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, journal, outbox>>

AnyHandBack == \E t \in Techs, b \in Boxes : HandBack(t, b)

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Techs, b \in Boxes : ReadTag(t, b) \/ QueuePush(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : Swap(t) \/ TearUpRead(t)
  \/ \E p \in outbox : LandPush(p) \/ BinPush(p)
  \/ AnyHandBack
  \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxWindow : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(AnyHandBack)

\* Price sheets are written into a box's journal in strictly rising generation
\* order, so nothing signed under a superseded tag ever lands on top.
JournalStrictlyRises ==
  \A b \in Boxes :
    \A i \in 1 .. (Len(journal[b]) - 1) :
      journal[b][i].gen < journal[b][i + 1].gen

EveryServiceEnds ==
  \A b \in Boxes : (tag[b].who # "none") ~> (tag[b].who = "none")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Boxes = {kiosk1, kiosk2}
    Techs = {tech1, tech2}
    MaxGen = 2
    MaxWindow = 1
    MaxFlight = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT JournalStrictlyRises

PROPERTY EveryServiceEnds

CONSTRAINT BoundedFlight

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A vending operator lets field technicians service its kiosks, and who is servicing which kiosk is settled by a single compare-and-swap tag on each kiosk. The tag holds the name of the technician currently on the box, or nothing if the box is free, along with a generation number that goes up by one every time the box is taken.

A technician reads a box's tag and remembers what it said. To actually take the box the technician swaps the tag: this only goes through if the tag still reads exactly what was read, namely free and at the same generation. If the tag has moved on, or somebody else got there first, or the dispatcher's service window has no room, the technician simply tears up the read and can go and read again.

The dispatcher sets how many boxes may be under service at once, and changes that number while the day runs; narrowing it can leave a read with nowhere to go, and it gets torn up like any other failed swap.

A technician on a box queues up a price sheet stamped with the generation the tag showed when it was queued. Sheets travel over the fleet network and can turn up at the box long after their author has handed the tag back and somebody else has taken the box. That is why the box only writes a sheet into its journal if the sheet's generation beats the generation of the last sheet it wrote; a sheet that does not beat it is binned. A technician hands a box back by clearing its name off the tag, leaving the generation where it is.

The full action set is: read a box's tag, swap the tag to take the box when the read still holds and the window has room, tear up a read that can no longer be swapped, queue a price sheet stamped with the current generation, land a sheet whose generation beats the box's last, bin a sheet that does not, hand a box back, and resize the service window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Each kiosk's journal records price sheets in strictly rising generation order, so a sheet written under a superseded tag never lands on top of a newer one.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every kiosk that is taken under service is eventually handed back.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m4p5t0 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Blocks, Crews, QueueCap

VARIABLES queue, hand, latched, onDuty, parked
vars == <<queue, hand, latched, onDuty, parked>>

Queued(b) == \E i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[i] = b
InSystem(b) == Queued(b) \/ b \in parked \/ \E c \in Crews : hand[c] = b

TypeOK ==
  /\ hand \in [Crews -> Blocks \cup {"none"}]
  /\ latched \in [Blocks -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ onDuty \in [Crews -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ parked \subseteq Blocks

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ hand = [c \in Crews |-> "none"]
  /\ latched = [b \in Blocks |-> FALSE]
  /\ onDuty = [c \in Crews |-> TRUE]
  /\ parked = {}

\* A trip order is only raised for a block that has nothing outstanding and has
\* not already been latched out.
RaiseOrder(b) ==
  /\ ~latched[b]
  /\ ~InSystem(b)
  /\ parked' = parked \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, hand, latched, onDuty>>

\* Backpressure: orders sit parked at the desk while the work queue is full.
Admit(b) ==
  /\ b \in parked
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
  /\ parked' = parked \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hand, latched, onDuty>>

TakeOrder(c) ==
  /\ onDuty[c]
  /\ hand[c] = "none"
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![c] = Head(queue)]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<latched, onDuty, parked>>

\* Firing the latch and closing the order are one indivisible step; that is what
\* stops a crew from dying in between and having the order handed out again.
FireLatch(c) ==
  /\ onDuty[c]
  /\ hand[c] \in Blocks
  /\ ~latched[hand[c]]
  /\ latched' = [latched EXCEPT ![hand[c]] = TRUE]
  /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, onDuty, parked>>

GoSilent(c) ==
  /\ onDuty[c]
  /\ onDuty' = [onDuty EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, hand, latched, parked>>

Recover(c) ==
  /\ ~onDuty[c]
  /\ hand[c] \in Blocks
  /\ parked' = parked \cup {hand[c]}
  /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, latched, onDuty>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : RaiseOrder(b) \/ Admit(b)
  \/ \E c \in Crews : TakeOrder(c) \/ FireLatch(c) \/ GoSilent(c) \/ Recover(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A latched block has nothing left anywhere in the system -- not parked at the
\* desk, not in the queue, not in anybody's hand -- so it cannot be fired twice.
LatchedBlockHasNothingOutstanding ==
  \A b \in Blocks : latched[b] => ~InSystem(b)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {blkA, blkB, blkC}
    Crews = {crew1, crew2}
    QueueCap = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LatchedBlockHasNothingOutstanding

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks, and each block has a one-shot emergency latch that cuts traction power to it. Firing that latch is irreversible for the shift: resetting it needs a maintenance crew on site with a key, so once a block is latched out it stays latched out.

Trip orders are handled through a work queue with a hard length limit. A controller raises a trip order for a block only when that block has nothing outstanding anywhere -- nothing parked at the desk, nothing sitting in the queue, nothing in a crew's hand -- and only when the block has not already been latched out. A raised order parks at the desk. Orders move from the desk onto the work queue when the queue has room; when the queue is full they simply stay parked, which is the whole of the backpressure story here.

A crew on duty with empty hands takes the order at the front of the queue. Firing the latch and closing out the order happen as one indivisible step: the block latches and the order leaves the crew's hand together. That indivisibility is what stops a crew from dying in between and having the same order handed out to somebody else afterwards.

A crew can go silent at any moment without warning and without saying what it was holding. The desk eventually notices a silent crew still holding an order and puts that order back on the desk to be queued again -- which is safe precisely because a crew that had already fired its latch would not still be holding anything.

The full action set is: raise a trip order for a block with nothing outstanding and no latch fired, admit a parked order onto the queue when there is room, take the front order off the queue, fire the latch and close the order in one step, go silent, and recover an order still held by a silent crew back onto the desk.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A block whose latch has been fired has nothing outstanding anywhere in the system -- not parked, not queued, not in any crew's hand -- so its latch can never be fired a second time.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m2p1t5 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Entries

VARIABLES chart, stage, ballot, told
vars == <<chart, stage, ballot, told>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ chart \in [Desks -> SUBSET Entries]
  /\ stage \in [Entries -> {"fresh", "polling", "standing", "dropped"}]
  /\ ballot \in [Entries -> [Desks -> {"quiet", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ told \subseteq Entries

Init ==
  /\ chart = [d \in Desks |-> {}]
  /\ stage = [e \in Entries |-> "fresh"]
  /\ ballot = [e \in Entries |-> [d \in Desks |-> "quiet"]]
  /\ told = {}

OpenPoll(e) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "fresh"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![e] = "polling"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, ballot, told>>

\* A yes vote writes the line into that desk's chart straight away, on the
\* understanding that it comes back out again if the entry is dropped.
VoteYes(e, d) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "polling"
  /\ ballot[e][d] = "quiet"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![e][d] = "yes"]
  /\ chart' = [chart EXCEPT ![d] = chart[d] \cup {e}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, told>>

VoteNo(e, d) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "polling"
  /\ ballot[e][d] = "quiet"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![e][d] = "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, stage, told>>

Stand(e) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "polling"
  /\ \A d \in Desks : ballot[e][d] = "yes"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![e] = "standing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, ballot, told>>

Drop(e) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "polling"
  /\ \E d \in Desks : ballot[e][d] = "no"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![e] = "dropped"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, ballot, told>>

\* The pharmacist in charge can push an entry through over a refusal, or pull
\* one that is still being polled. Neither override touches a standing entry.
OverrideStand(e) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "polling"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![e] = "standing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, ballot, told>>

OverrideDrop(e) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "polling"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![e] = "dropped"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, ballot, told>>

BackFill(e, d) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "standing"
  /\ e \notin chart[d]
  /\ chart' = [chart EXCEPT ![d] = chart[d] \cup {e}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, ballot, told>>

RollBack(e, d) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "dropped"
  /\ e \in chart[d]
  /\ chart' = [chart EXCEPT ![d] = chart[d] \ {e}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, ballot, told>>

TellPatient(e) ==
  /\ stage[e] = "standing"
  /\ \A d \in Desks : e \in chart[d]
  /\ told' = told \cup {e}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, stage, ballot>>

Settle ==
  \/ \E e \in Entries, d \in Desks : VoteYes(e, d) \/ VoteNo(e, d)
  \/ \E e \in Entries : Stand(e) \/ Drop(e)

Next ==
  \/ \E e \in Entries : OpenPoll(e) \/ OverrideStand(e) \/ OverrideDrop(e)
  \/ Settle
  \/ \E e \in Entries, d \in Desks : BackFill(e, d) \/ RollBack(e, d)
  \/ \E e \in Entries : TellPatient(e)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Settle)

\* Anything the patient has been told is on file is on every desk's chart.
NoToldEntryMissing ==
  \A d \in Desks : told \subseteq chart[d]

EveryPollDecided ==
  \A e \in Entries :
    (stage[e] = "polling") ~> (stage[e] \in {"standing", "dropped"})
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Desks = {robot, counter, insurer}
    Entries = {rx1, rx2}

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoToldEntryMissing

PROPERTY EveryPollDecided

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A pharmacy keeps a patient's medication chart in three places that must not drift apart: the dispensing robot, the counter terminal, and the insurer link. Adding a line to the chart is settled as a two-phase commit over those three desks.

A new line starts fresh and is put out to poll. A desk that votes yes writes the line into its own copy of the chart there and then, on the understanding that it comes back out again if the line is dropped. A desk that votes no writes nothing. The line stands once all three desks have voted yes, and is dropped if any desk voted no.

The pharmacist in charge has an override. She can make a line stand over a desk's refusal -- which is what happens when the insurer link refuses a drug the patient plainly needs -- and she can pull a line that is still being polled. Neither override touches a line that already stands: once a line stands it stays standing.

A desk that has not got a standing line in its copy back-fills it, which is how a desk that voted no or never voted at all catches up after an override. A desk that has a dropped line in its copy takes it back out again. The patient is told a line is on file only once the line stands and every one of the three desks has it in its copy.

The full action set is: put a fresh line out to poll, vote yes and write the line into that desk's copy, vote no, let a line stand on a full set of yes votes, drop a line that got a no, override a polling line into standing, override a polling line into dropped, back-fill a standing line into a desk that lacks it, take a dropped line back out of a desk's copy, and tell the patient about a standing line that every desk has.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every line the patient has been told is on file is present in all three desks' copies of the chart, so no acknowledged update is ever lost from any copy.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every line put out to poll eventually ends up either standing or dropped.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od1m8p4t0 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Strips, AreaCap

VARIABLES apron, strip, spot, tally, powered
vars == <<apron, strip, spot, tally, powered>>

OnArea == {f \in Flights : spot[f] \in {"taxiing", "linedup"}}
HoldsStrip(f) == \E r \in Strips : strip[r] = f

TypeOK ==
  /\ apron \in Flights \cup {"free"}
  /\ strip \in [Strips -> Flights \cup {"free"}]
  /\ spot \in [Flights -> {"stand", "taxiing", "linedup", "away"}]
  /\ tally \in 0 .. AreaCap
  /\ powered \in [Flights -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ apron = "free"
  /\ strip = [r \in Strips |-> "free"]
  /\ spot = [f \in Flights |-> "stand"]
  /\ tally = 0
  /\ powered = [f \in Flights |-> TRUE]

TakeApron(f) ==
  /\ powered[f]
  /\ spot[f] = "stand"
  /\ apron = "free"
  /\ apron' = f
  /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, spot, tally, powered>>

\* Only the apron holder may push the movement tally, so the count and the metal
\* on the ground move together and cannot drift apart.
PushOff(f) ==
  /\ powered[f]
  /\ apron = f
  /\ spot[f] = "stand"
  /\ tally < AreaCap
  /\ tally' = tally + 1
  /\ spot' = [spot EXCEPT ![f] = "taxiing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<apron, strip, powered>>

\* Hand over hand: the strip lock is taken before the apron lock is let go, so
\* the two levels are never grabbed in the other order.
CoupleToStrip(f, r) ==
  /\ powered[f]
  /\ apron = f
  /\ spot[f] = "taxiing"
  /\ strip[r] = "free"
  /\ strip' = [strip EXCEPT ![r] = f]
  /\ apron' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spot, tally, powered>>

LineUp(f) ==
  /\ powered[f]
  /\ spot[f] = "taxiing"
  /\ HoldsStrip(f)
  /\ spot' = [spot EXCEPT ![f] = "linedup"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<apron, strip, tally, powered>>

Roll(f) ==
  /\ powered[f]
  /\ spot[f] = "linedup"
  /\ spot' = [spot EXCEPT ![f] = "away"]
  /\ strip' = [r \in Strips |-> IF strip[r] = f THEN "free" ELSE strip[r]]
  /\ tally' = tally - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<apron, powered>>

\* A dead aircraft keeps its locks and, more to the point, keeps its metal on
\* the movement area until somebody physically drags it off.
GoDead(f) ==
  /\ powered[f]
  /\ powered' = [powered EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<apron, strip, spot, tally>>

Tow(f) ==
  /\ ~powered[f]
  /\ spot[f] \in {"taxiing", "linedup"}
  /\ spot' = [spot EXCEPT ![f] = "away"]
  /\ strip' = [r \in Strips |-> IF strip[r] = f THEN "free" ELSE strip[r]]
  /\ apron' = IF apron = f THEN "free" ELSE apron
  /\ tally' = tally - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED powered

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Flights :
       TakeApron(f) \/ PushOff(f) \/ LineUp(f) \/ Roll(f) \/ GoDead(f) \/ Tow(f)
  \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Strips : CoupleToStrip(f, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Never more aircraft actually out on the movement area than it is rated for.
MovementAreaWithinCap == Cardinality(OnArea) <= AreaCap
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Flights = {af101, af202, af303}
    Strips = {strip1, strip2}
    AreaCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MovementAreaWithinCap

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airfield's ground movement is rated for only so many aircraft out on the manoeuvring area at once. Access is governed by two levels of lock, always taken coarse first and fine second: there is one apron lock covering the whole movement area, and one strip lock for each departure strip.

An aircraft at its stand takes the apron lock. Holding the apron lock, it pushes off: the movement tally goes up by one and the aircraft is now taxiing out on the area. Only the holder of the apron lock is allowed to push the tally, which is what keeps the tally and the metal actually on the ground moving together instead of drifting apart. A taxiing aircraft then couples to a free strip hand over hand -- it takes the strip lock first and only then lets go of the apron lock, so the two levels are never grabbed in the opposite order and nothing can end up waiting on a cycle. With a strip in hand the aircraft lines up, and from lined up it rolls: it leaves the area, the strip lock is dropped, and the tally comes down by one.

An aircraft can go dead on the ground without warning -- no radio, no movement, nothing. A dead aircraft keeps whatever locks it was holding and, far more to the point, keeps its metal sitting out on the manoeuvring area. It stays there until a tug physically drags it off, and that tow is what drops its locks and brings the tally down; dropping the tally for an aircraft that is still sitting out there would be exactly the wrong thing to do.

The full action set is: take the apron lock at the stand, push off onto the area under the apron lock, couple to a free strip and release the apron lock, line up on the held strip, roll and clear the area, go dead on the ground, and tow a dead aircraft off the area.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of aircraft actually out on the manoeuvring area never exceeds what the area is rated for.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od3m4p6t5 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Members, Batches, QueueCap, MaxSerial

VARIABLES queue, mandate, lodged, settled, window
vars == <<queue, mandate, lodged, settled, window>>

Standing(m, s) == mandate[m].state = "live" /\ mandate[m].serial = s
Waiting(k) == \E i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[i].tkt = k

TypeOK ==
  /\ mandate \in [Members -> [state : {"live", "pulled"}, serial : 0 .. MaxSerial]]
  /\ lodged \subseteq Batches
  /\ settled \subseteq Batches
  /\ window \in {"open", "shut"}

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ mandate = [m \in Members |-> [state |-> "live", serial |-> 0]]
  /\ lodged = {}
  /\ settled = {}
  /\ window = "open"

\* Backpressure: a member with a live mandate simply cannot lodge while the
\* settlement queue is at its length limit.
Lodge(k, m) ==
  /\ k \notin lodged
  /\ mandate[m].state = "live"
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, [bank |-> m, serial |-> mandate[m].serial, tkt |-> k])
  /\ lodged' = lodged \cup {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mandate, settled, window>>

SettleHead ==
  /\ window = "open"
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ settled' = settled \cup {Head(queue).tkt}
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mandate, lodged, window>>

\* The duty officer's overrides. Pulling a mandate scrubs that member's batches
\* out of the queue in the same stroke; leaving them there is the whole bug.
PullMandate(m) ==
  /\ mandate[m].state = "live"
  /\ mandate[m].serial < MaxSerial
  /\ mandate' = [mandate EXCEPT ![m] =
        [state |-> "pulled", serial |-> mandate[m].serial + 1]]
  /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA e : e.bank # m)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lodged, settled, window>>

Reinstate(m) ==
  /\ mandate[m].state = "pulled"
  /\ mandate[m].serial < MaxSerial
  /\ mandate' = [mandate EXCEPT ![m] =
        [state |-> "live", serial |-> mandate[m].serial + 1]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, lodged, settled, window>>

ShutWindow ==
  /\ window = "open"
  /\ window' = "shut"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, mandate, lodged, settled>>

OpenWindow ==
  /\ window = "shut"
  /\ window' = "open"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, mandate, lodged, settled>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Batches, m \in Members : Lodge(k, m)
  \/ SettleHead
  \/ \E m \in Members : PullMandate(m) \/ Reinstate(m)
  \/ ShutWindow
  \/ OpenWindow

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(OpenWindow)
  /\ SF_vars(SettleHead)

\* Nothing stale is ever left sitting in the settlement queue.
QueueHoldsOnlyStandingBatches ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : Standing(queue[i].bank, queue[i].serial)

EveryLodgedBatchLeaves == \A k \in Batches : Waiting(k) ~> ~Waiting(k)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Members = {northBank, southBank}
    Batches = {bt1, bt2, bt3}
    QueueCap = 2
    MaxSerial = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT QueueHoldsOnlyStandingBatches

PROPERTY EveryLodgedBatchLeaves

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A central bank runs interbank settlement in batches. Member banks lodge batches into a settlement queue that has a hard length limit; when the queue is at that limit a member simply cannot lodge, however urgent its batch, and has to wait for the queue to drain. That is the whole of the backpressure arrangement.

A member may only lodge while its mandate to settle is live, and every lodged batch is stamped with the serial of the mandate it was lodged under. Batches leave the queue from the front: while the settlement window is open the batch at the head is put through and marked settled.

The duty officer at the central bank has overrides that ordinary members do not. She can pull a member's mandate, which marks it pulled and moves it to a new serial; pulling a mandate scrubs that member's batches out of the settlement queue in the same stroke, because a batch lodged under a mandate that no longer stands must not be sitting there waiting to be put through. She can reinstate a pulled mandate, again on a new serial, after which the member may lodge afresh. She can also shut the settlement window and open it again, which stops and restarts the draining of the queue without touching anything in it.

The full action set is: lodge a batch under a live mandate while the queue is below its limit, settle the batch at the head of the queue while the window is open, pull a member's mandate and scrub its batches from the queue, reinstate a pulled mandate on a new serial, shut the settlement window, and open the settlement window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every batch sitting in the settlement queue was lodged under a mandate that still stands today at exactly the serial it was stamped with, so nothing lodged by a member whose mandate has been pulled or superseded is ever waiting to settle.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every batch that reaches the settlement queue eventually leaves it.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od1m6p6t3 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Runways, Flights, Span, Skew, WallEnd, MaxSlips

NoSlip == [rwy |-> "none", num |-> 0, ac |-> "none", from |-> 0, to |-> 0]

VARIABLES wall, panel, slips, carried, rolls
vars == <<wall, panel, slips, carried, rolls>>

ValidNow(r) == \E c \in slips : c.rwy = r /\ wall < c.to

TypeOK ==
  /\ wall \in 0 .. WallEnd
  /\ panel \in [Flights -> 0 .. WallEnd]
  /\ carried \in [Flights -> [rwy : Runways \cup {"none"}, num : Nat,
                              ac : Flights \cup {"none"}, from : Nat, to : Nat]]

Init ==
  /\ wall = 0
  /\ panel = [f \in Flights |-> 0]
  /\ slips = {}
  /\ carried = [f \in Flights |-> NoSlip]
  /\ rolls = {}

\* Cockpit panels lag the tower wall clock, but never by more than the certified
\* skew, and they always keep creeping up -- a slow flight, not a lost one.
TowerTick ==
  /\ wall < WallEnd
  /\ \A f \in Flights : (wall + 1) - panel[f] <= Skew
  /\ wall' = wall + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<panel, slips, carried, rolls>>

PanelCatchUp(f) ==
  /\ panel[f] < wall
  /\ panel' = [panel EXCEPT ![f] = panel[f] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wall, slips, carried, rolls>>

\* The tower will not cut a new slip for a runway while an old one is still
\* inside its window, so slips on one runway never overlap in time.
CutSlip(r, f) ==
  /\ Cardinality(slips) < MaxSlips
  /\ ~ValidNow(r)
  /\ slips' = slips \cup {[rwy |-> r, num |-> Cardinality(slips) + 1, ac |-> f,
                           from |-> wall, to |-> wall + Span]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wall, panel, carried, rolls>>

RadioSlip(f, c) ==
  /\ c \in slips
  /\ c.ac = f
  /\ carried[f] # c
  /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![f] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wall, panel, slips, rolls>>

\* The crew reads its own panel and leaves a whole skew of margin before the
\* slip runs out; that margin is the only thing making the roll legal in tower
\* time rather than merely in cockpit time.
RollOut(f) ==
  /\ carried[f].rwy \in Runways
  /\ panel[f] >= carried[f].from
  /\ panel[f] + Skew < carried[f].to
  /\ rolls' = rolls \cup {[rwy |-> carried[f].rwy, num |-> carried[f].num,
                           ac |-> f, at |-> wall]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wall, panel, slips, carried>>

Next ==
  \/ TowerTick
  \/ \E f \in Flights : PanelCatchUp(f) \/ RollOut(f)
  \/ \E r \in Runways, f \in Flights : CutSlip(r, f)
  \/ \E f \in Flights, c \in slips : RadioSlip(f, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every roll traces to a slip cut to that flight, and happened inside its window
\* as the tower clock saw it -- not merely as the cockpit saw it.
NoUnauthorizedRoll ==
  \A m \in rolls :
    \E c \in slips :
      /\ c.rwy = m.rwy
      /\ c.num = m.num
      /\ c.ac = m.ac
      /\ m.at >= c.from
      /\ m.at < c.to
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Runways = {r09, r27}
    Flights = {ba12, kl88}
    Span = 3
    Skew = 1
    WallEnd = 3
    MaxSlips = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedRoll

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport tower allocates its runways by cutting timed slips. A slip names one runway, one flight, a slip number, the tower wall-clock reading it was cut at, and the reading it runs out at. The tower will not cut a new slip for a runway while an older slip for that runway is still inside its window, so the slips on any one runway never overlap in time.

Cockpit panels do not read the same time as the tower. A panel always trails the tower wall clock, and the certification rule is that it never trails by more than a fixed skew; the tower will not advance its own clock past the point where some panel would fall further behind than that. Panels creep forward towards the tower reading on their own. A flight is never treated as lost, only as slow: its panel is behind, and it will catch up.

A slip reaches a flight by radio, and that can happen at any point after it was cut, including well after the window it describes has already run out. A flight carries whatever slip reached it most recently.

To roll onto a runway a crew works entirely from its own panel, because that is all it has. It requires that its panel has reached the start of the slip's window, and, crucially, that its panel plus a full skew of margin is still short of the end of that window. That margin is the whole point: it is what makes the roll legal in tower time and not merely in cockpit time. Every roll is recorded by the tower with the runway, the flight, the slip number quoted, and the tower wall-clock reading at the moment it happened.

The full action set is: advance the tower wall clock while no panel would fall outside the certified skew, creep a lagging cockpit panel forward, cut a slip for a runway with no slip currently inside its window, radio an already-cut slip to the flight it names, and roll out on the carried slip when the panel plus a skew of margin is still inside the window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every recorded roll matches a slip that the tower actually cut for that flight on that runway, and the tower's own clock reading at the moment of the roll falls inside that slip's window -- so no flight ever acts on a slip that was not its own or that had already run out.
